session_1.speaker: Isak
session_1.text: Hey you! Finally got a free evening to chat. How's the week been?

session_1.speaker: Maren
session_1.text: Long but fine. Work has been hectic at Mossgate Studio, we've got a big deadline coming up, but I survived.

session_1.speaker: Isak
session_1.text: Ha, survived is the key word. Did you at least get outside at all this weekend?

session_1.speaker: Maren
session_1.text: Yes! I finally did that ridge trail you kept recommending. The first half is brutal uphill but the view at the top made up for it.

session_1.speaker: Isak
session_1.text: Told you! Did you do the loop back through the pine section? That part is my favorite.

session_1.speaker: Maren
session_1.text: I did, and my knees were not thrilled by the end. I basically hobbled to the car.

session_1.speaker: Isak
session_1.text: Worth it though. Oh, did you hear Tove and Anders finally set a date for the wedding?

session_1.speaker: Maren
session_1.text: I did, it's on a farm somewhere out in the countryside, right? I'm excited, I just have no idea what to wear.

session_1.speaker: Isak
session_1.text: Same. I'm told it's semi-formal, which means nothing to me. I'll probably just panic-buy a jacket the week before.

session_1.speaker: Maren
session_1.text: Classic you. Speaking of panic, I tried making a risotto last night and it turned into something closer to glue.

session_1.speaker: Isak
session_1.text: Oh no. Did you add all the stock at once? That's the usual crime.

session_1.speaker: Maren
session_1.text: Absolutely guilty. I got distracted by my phone and by the time I looked up it was a solid brick of rice. We ended up eating toast.

session_1.speaker: Isak
session_1.text: Toast dinner is underrated, honestly. I do it at least once a week and don't regret it.

session_1.speaker: Maren
session_1.text: Fair. Oh, I also picked up a new plant on the way home yesterday, the pothos. It's already trailing off my bookshelf like it owns the place.

session_1.speaker: Isak
session_1.text: Nice, those are hard to kill, which is perfect for you. Send me a picture once it's settled in.

session_1.speaker: Maren
session_1.text: Will do. Alright, I should go figure out dinner that isn't toast. Talk in a couple of weeks?

session_1.speaker: Isak
session_1.text: Sounds good. Good luck with the deadline, and with not burning anything!

session_2.speaker: Maren
session_2.text: Hey you! Finally got a quiet evening, so I'm on the sofa with tea and nothing planned. How's your week been?

session_2.speaker: Isak
session_2.text: Pretty slow, which I'm not complaining about. I've been daydreaming about a holiday though, maybe somewhere with mountains and no phone signal.

session_2.speaker: Maren
session_2.text: Ooh yes. I keep going back and forth between a lazy beach week and a proper hiking trip. Probably I'd get bored on the beach by day three.

session_2.speaker: Isak
session_2.text: Same. Maybe a road trip would be the compromise, a bit of coast, a bit of hills, and no fixed plan.

session_2.speaker: Maren
session_2.text: Road trip sounds right. Funny enough I only have a small boot to work with, I drive a Honda Jazz, so we'd have to pack light.

session_2.speaker: Isak
session_2.text: Packing light is a good rule anyway. Did you watch anything good lately? I finally saw that old sci-fi film everyone raves about.

session_2.speaker: Maren
session_2.text: Wait, I need to fix something I just said. I don't drive a Honda Jazz, that was a slip on my part, it's a Volvo V60. Much bigger boot, so maybe packing light isn't a rule after all.

session_2.speaker: Isak
session_2.text: Ha, that's a pretty big slip, those are very different cars. Fine, you're officially in charge of luggage on the road trip then.

session_2.speaker: Maren
session_2.text: Deal. Okay, tell me about the film, was it worth the hype?

session_2.speaker: Isak
session_2.text: Mostly yes. The first hour is slow but the ending stuck with me for days, and the soundtrack is unreal. I'd watch it again just for that.

session_2.speaker: Maren
session_2.text: Adding it to my list. I've been in a rut with films, I keep rewatching the same comfort ones.

session_2.speaker: Isak
session_2.text: Nothing wrong with comfort films. I do the same with cooking, actually, and last weekend that went badly. I tried a creamy pasta bake and the sauce split into this greasy mess.

session_2.speaker: Maren
session_2.text: Oh no. Did you add the cheese when it was too hot? That's what usually does it to me.

session_2.speaker: Isak
session_2.text: Probably, I was impatient and just dumped it all in. We ended up eating toast with the rescued noodles on the side.

session_2.speaker: Maren
session_2.text: Honestly that sounds like a decent dinner. Next time take the pan off the heat first and stir the cheese in slowly.

session_2.speaker: Isak
session_2.text: Noted, I'll try again this weekend. Talk in a couple of weeks? I want to hear where the road trip planning goes.

session_2.speaker: Maren
session_2.text: Definitely. I'll start collecting ideas. Sleep well!

session_3.speaker: Maren
session_3.text: Hey you! Survived the weekend? I spent most of mine catching up on sleep, which feels very grown up and very sad.

session_3.speaker: Isak
session_3.text: Ha, same energy here. I mostly lay on the sofa and listened to that podcast I told you about, the one with the two guys who investigate old local mysteries.

session_3.speaker: Maren
session_3.text: Oh the one about the missing lighthouse keeper? I started it on Friday, I'm only two episodes in but I'm hooked.

session_3.speaker: Isak
session_3.text: Yes that's the one! Don't skip ahead, episode five has a twist I did not see coming.

session_3.speaker: Maren
session_3.text: No spoilers, I'm warning you. Anyway, big news on my end, I finally switched jobs, I'm at Halvorsen Freight now and so far the people seem really decent.

session_3.speaker: Isak
session_3.text: Wait, congrats! That's great, I want the full story next time. Is the commute any better at least?

session_3.speaker: Maren
session_3.text: Marginally. I'll tell you everything soon, but right now my brain is full of wedding logistics for Tove and Anders.

session_3.speaker: Isak
session_3.text: Right, the wedding! Have you figured out what you're wearing? I'm still staring at a suit that I think shrank in the closet.

session_3.speaker: Maren
session_3.text: Suits don't shrink, Isak, you just ate well over winter. I'm wearing the green dress, finally found shoes that don't destroy my feet.

session_3.speaker: Isak
session_3.text: Fair, fair. I hear they've booked a band instead of a DJ, so there's going to be actual dancing and no hiding.

session_3.speaker: Maren
session_3.text: Terrifying. Also, unrelated, I bought a new plant on Saturday, the fiddle-leaf fig, and it's already dropping one leaf out of spite.

session_3.speaker: Isak
session_3.text: Those things are divas, I've heard. Mine would be dead in a week, I can barely keep a basil plant going.

session_3.speaker: Maren
session_3.text: I'm giving it the brightest corner and talking to it nicely. Meanwhile the neighbour upstairs decided 11pm was a good time to move furniture last night.

session_3.speaker: Isak
session_3.text: Ugh, the noisy neighbour saga continues. Did you knock on the door or just stew silently like a normal person?

session_3.speaker: Maren
session_3.text: Stewed silently, obviously. My sister Ingrid says I should leave a polite note, but I'm more of a passive-aggressive ceiling-thumping type.

session_3.speaker: Isak
session_3.text: Honestly the note is the classier move. Try it, and if that fails, we escalate to thumping together.

session_3.speaker: Maren
session_3.text: Deal. Okay, I need to go make dinner, talk in a couple of weeks? And report back on episode five.

session_4.speaker: Maren
session_4.text: Hey you. Sorry I went quiet, the last couple of weeks have been a blur.

session_4.speaker: Isak
session_4.text: No worries, I've been bad at replying too. How's everything otherwise?

session_4.speaker: Maren
session_4.text: Mostly fine except the neighbour upstairs. He started practising drums at ten at night. Drums! Who does that?

session_4.speaker: Isak
session_4.text: Oh no. Have you said anything to him yet or are you still in the passive-aggressive sigh phase?

session_4.speaker: Maren
session_4.text: Sigh phase. I left a very polite note and he responded by playing quieter for exactly one evening.

session_4.speaker: Isak
session_4.text: Classic. Did you get the wedding invitation, by the way? Dagny's, I mean.

session_4.speaker: Maren
session_4.text: Yes! It came last week. I'm so happy for them, though I'm already nervous about the dinner, because I'm allergic to shellfish and weddings love a seafood starter.

session_4.speaker: Isak
session_4.text: Good point, you should flag that on the RSVP. They're pretty organised, they'll sort you out something.

session_4.speaker: Maren
session_4.text: That's what I figured. I'll tick the box and hope for the best. Are you going to give a speech or just heckle?

session_4.speaker: Isak
session_4.text: Heckle, obviously. Although I did get asked to say a few words at the rehearsal thing, so I need to come up with something not embarrassing.

session_4.speaker: Maren
session_4.text: Ha, good luck with that. Tell the story about the broken tent at the festival.

session_4.speaker: Isak
session_4.text: That's the embarrassing one! But yeah, it might work if I keep it short.

session_4.speaker: Maren
session_4.text: Anyway, I started a new podcast on my commute that you'd probably like. It's two historians arguing about famous bridges, weirdly gripping.

session_4.speaker: Isak
session_4.text: Bridges? That sounds oddly perfect. Send me the name and I'll give it a go on my run tomorrow.

session_4.speaker: Maren
session_4.text: Will do, I'll text it over in a sec. Fair warning, the hosts bicker a lot.

session_4.speaker: Isak
session_4.text: Bickering is a feature, not a bug. Talk soon, and good luck with the drummer.

session_5.speaker: Isak
session_5.text: Hey you! Survived the long weekend? I basically did nothing, which was glorious.

session_5.speaker: Maren
session_5.text: Same, mostly. I had a dentist appointment this morning, so the weekend's good mood has officially worn off.

session_5.speaker: Isak
session_5.text: Ugh, sorry. Is that the same one you've been going to for ages?

session_5.speaker: Maren
session_5.text: Yep, still Dr. Okafor. She's great, I just hate the scraping sound.

session_5.speaker: Isak
session_5.text: Fair. Anyway, I finally watched that slow Icelandic film everyone was raving about. Two hours of a man staring at sheep, and somehow I loved it.

session_5.speaker: Maren
session_5.text: Ha, that sounds exactly like something you'd love. Was it the one with the long shots of the highlands?

session_5.speaker: Isak
session_5.text: That's the one. The landscape alone carries it, honestly. It made me want to go outside and walk for a week.

session_5.speaker: Maren
session_5.text: Funny you say that, I did the ridge trail on Saturday, the one with the stone steps at the start. The views from the top were unreal, and almost nobody was there.

session_5.speaker: Isak
session_5.text: Jealous. My knees are still complaining about the last time I tried steps like that. Was it muddy?

session_5.speaker: Maren
session_5.text: Only the first bit, then it dries out. Bring proper boots and you'll be fine.

session_5.speaker: Isak
session_5.text: Noted. Should I be watching anything this week? I need something for the evenings.

session_5.speaker: Maren
session_5.text: I've been working through a miniseries on Lumen, since I subscribe there anyway. It's short and moody, very much your taste.

session_5.speaker: Isak
session_5.text: I might borrow a free trial and check it out. Have you been listening to anything good lately?

session_5.speaker: Maren
session_5.text: Yes! A podcast about forgotten inventions. Each episode is about some doomed gadget from a hundred years ago, and it's weirdly addictive.

session_5.speaker: Isak
session_5.text: Oh that sounds fun, I'll queue it up for the commute tomorrow.

session_5.speaker: Maren
session_5.text: Do it. Then we can compare favourite doomed gadgets next time.

session_6.speaker: Isak
session_6.text: Hey you! Survived the week? I finally watched that old noir film everyone keeps going on about last night.

session_6.speaker: Maren
session_6.text: Hey! Mostly survived, yes. Oh nice, which one? Was it as moody as people say?

session_6.speaker: Isak
session_6.text: Extremely moody. Lots of rain, lots of cigarettes, a detective who never smiles once. I loved it, though the ending made no sense to me.

session_6.speaker: Maren
session_6.text: Haha, that's the genre, the ending is never supposed to make sense. I've been meaning to watch something like that, I need a proper cozy night in.

session_6.speaker: Isak
session_6.text: Do it. Speaking of cozy, how's the flat looking these days? Last time you were saying it felt a bit empty.

session_6.speaker: Maren
session_6.text: Better, actually. I picked up the peace lily from a little market stall on Saturday, and it already makes the corner by the window feel less bare.

session_6.speaker: Isak
session_6.text: Nice, those look good even when you ignore them a bit. Did it go in the spot where your old plant was?

session_6.speaker: Maren
session_6.text: Yes, exactly that spot. The fiddle-leaf fig is gone, it dropped leaf after leaf for weeks and I finally had to admit defeat.

session_6.speaker: Isak
session_6.text: Ah, sorry. Fair enough though, you gave it a good run. Anyway, I'm trying to plan some kind of holiday for later this year and I have no ideas at all.

session_6.speaker: Maren
session_6.text: Ooh. Are you thinking beach, or more wandering around somewhere with good food and old streets?

session_6.speaker: Isak
session_6.text: Honestly the second one. Somewhere I can walk all day, sit in cafes, and not think about anything. Maybe a train trip instead of flying.

session_6.speaker: Maren
session_6.text: Train trips are the best, you actually get to watch the country change. I'd go for that over an airport any day.

session_6.speaker: Isak
session_6.text: Agreed. I'd just like to sleep properly first. My neighbour upstairs has started dragging furniture around at midnight, I swear.

session_6.speaker: Maren
session_6.text: Oh no, the classic. Have you said anything, or are you doing the passive-aggressive broom-on-the-ceiling thing?

session_6.speaker: Isak
session_6.text: Broom stage, sadly. I might leave a polite note first, but it's hard to stay polite at one in the morning.

session_6.speaker: Maren
session_6.text: Write the note when you're well rested, it'll come out nicer. Let me know how it goes!

session_7.speaker: Isak
session_7.text: Hey you. Finally got round to watching that Icelandic film you recommended last time. I think I have to sit with it a few days before I know what I thought.

session_7.speaker: Maren
session_7.text: Ha, that's the right reaction honestly. Which part got you, the long silent stretches or the ending?

session_7.speaker: Isak
session_7.text: The silences, mostly. Every time I thought someone would finally say something, the camera just stayed on the landscape. Weirdly hypnotic though.

session_7.speaker: Maren
session_7.text: Right? I watched it half asleep the first time and it still worked on me. Oh, before I forget, book club is at Pilcrow Books again this month, same back-room table as usual.

session_7.speaker: Isak
session_7.text: Good, I like that room. I'll bring back the book I borrowed too, I'm only about two thirds through but I'll live.

session_7.speaker: Maren
session_7.text: Nobody's going to check, we mostly just talk about everything except the book anyway.

session_7.speaker: Isak
session_7.text: True. Anyway, I've been daydreaming about a summer holiday. Somewhere with a coastline and no real plan, just wandering.

session_7.speaker: Maren
session_7.text: That sounds lovely. I'd be tempted by somewhere green and a bit remote, a place where you can get lost in the hills for a few days.

session_7.speaker: Isak
session_7.text: Now you're talking. Speaking of hills, I did that ridge trail on Sunday, the one with the stone shelter at the top.

session_7.speaker: Maren
session_7.text: Oh nice, how was it? I've heard the last climb is brutal but the view makes up for it.

session_7.speaker: Isak
session_7.text: Brutal is fair. My knees complained the whole way down. But the view was ridiculous, you could see for miles, and it was almost empty because everyone sensibly stayed home.

session_7.speaker: Maren
session_7.text: I need to do that one soon. Oh, small news, I picked up a new plant this week, the monstera. It's already taking over the corner by the window.

session_7.speaker: Isak
session_7.text: Those things are dramatic in the best way. Does it have the split leaves yet or is it still in the baby phase?

session_7.speaker: Maren
session_7.text: Baby phase, but I'm optimistic. I keep checking it like it's going to grow overnight.

session_7.speaker: Isak
session_7.text: Send me a photo when it does. And let's pick a weekend for that trail, I'll even carry the snacks.

session_7.speaker: Maren
session_7.text: Deal. Snacks carrier is the best job. Talk soon!

session_8.speaker: Isak
session_8.text: Hey you. Survive the week? You mentioned last time your upstairs situation was getting rough.

session_8.speaker: Maren
session_8.text: Barely. The neighbour was running some kind of power tool at eleven last night. On a Monday. I stood there in my socks glaring at the ceiling like that would help.

session_8.speaker: Isak
session_8.text: Classic. Did you go up and say something?

session_8.speaker: Maren
session_8.text: I left a very polite note on their door instead. Passive aggression with a smiley face. We'll see if it works.

session_8.speaker: Isak
session_8.text: Bold strategy. Smiley faces are basically a threat.

session_8.speaker: Maren
session_8.text: Exactly the vibe I was going for. Oh, unrelated, I finally cancelled the Lumen subscription. I kept paying for it and barely opened it.

session_8.speaker: Isak
session_8.text: Ha, good for you. I have like three of those I keep meaning to kill off. Did you at least watch anything decent lately?

session_8.speaker: Maren
session_8.text: I saw an old film on a friend's couch, a slow Scandinavian thing about two brothers and a broken-down ferry. Sounds dull, but I couldn't look away.

session_8.speaker: Isak
session_8.text: That actually sounds like my kind of thing. Was it sad or just quietly bleak?

session_8.speaker: Maren
session_8.text: Quietly bleak with moments of surprisingly dry humour. The ending left me staring at the credits for a while.

session_8.speaker: Isak
session_8.text: Okay, adding it to my list. I've mostly been outside instead. Did the ridge trail on Saturday, the one with the long stone staircase near the start.

session_8.speaker: Maren
session_8.text: Oh nice, how was it? I've heard the staircase kills your legs.

session_8.speaker: Isak
session_8.text: It does, but the view at the top makes up for it. You can see right across the valley, and there was hardly anyone there.

session_8.speaker: Maren
session_8.text: Okay, now I want to go. Is it doable in a day without being a total slog?

session_8.speaker: Isak
session_8.text: Totally. Start early, bring more water than you think you need, and it's easy. Want to try it together sometime?

session_8.speaker: Maren
session_8.text: Yes, let's. Pick a weekend that isn't raining and I'm in. I'll even promise not to complain about the staircase.

session_9.speaker: Maren
session_9.text: Hey you! Finally sitting down with a coffee, how's your week been?

session_9.speaker: Isak
session_9.text: Pretty good, busy but fine. I've been daydreaming about a holiday though, anywhere that isn't my desk.

session_9.speaker: Maren
session_9.text: Ha, same. I keep flicking between a beach week and one of those slow train trips through the mountains.

session_9.speaker: Isak
session_9.text: Train trip sounds dreamy. I'd probably fall asleep with my face against the window, but happily.

session_9.speaker: Maren
session_9.text: Oh, random life update: I switched dentists recently and I'm with Dr. Abernathy now. Had my first check-up and it was oddly painless.

session_9.speaker: Isak
session_9.text: Painless is the dream with dentists. Glad it went well!

session_9.speaker: Maren
session_9.text: Right? Also I finally sorted out my phone situation and I'm paying $44 a month now, which feels like a win.

session_9.speaker: Isak
session_9.text: Nice, any saving is a good saving. I should really look at mine, I haven't in ages.

session_9.speaker: Maren
session_9.text: Do it, it only takes an evening. Anyway, are you going to Tove's wedding? I still can't believe she's actually tying the knot.

session_9.speaker: Isak
session_9.text: Wouldn't miss it. I heard it's an outdoor ceremony, so I'm hoping the weather behaves.

session_9.speaker: Maren
session_9.text: Fingers crossed. This weekend looks lovely at least, sunny all day Saturday apparently.

session_9.speaker: Isak
session_9.text: Perfect. I'm thinking a long walk and then lying in the grass doing nothing. Any plans on your end?

session_9.speaker: Maren
session_9.text: Tidying the flat mostly, since I've got a bit more space on the windowsill now that the monstera is gone. It didn't make it in the end.

session_9.speaker: Isak
session_9.text: Aw, sorry to hear that. Well, at least you get a sunnier windowsill out of it.

session_9.speaker: Maren
session_9.text: True! Okay, I'll let you get on with your day. Talk in a couple of weeks?

session_9.speaker: Isak
session_9.text: Definitely. Enjoy the sunshine and say hi to the weekend for me!

session_10.speaker: Isak
session_10.text: Hey, you alive? Feels like forever since we last talked.

session_10.speaker: Maren
session_10.text: Barely! It's been a week of heat and bad sleep. How are you doing?

session_10.speaker: Isak
session_10.text: Pretty good. I finally did that ridge trail I kept going on about, the one with the long gravel climb at the start.

session_10.speaker: Maren
session_10.text: Oh nice, how was it? Did the view actually make up for the climb?

session_10.speaker: Isak
session_10.text: Totally. Clear day, hardly anyone up there, and I sat at the top eating a very sad sandwich and felt great.

session_10.speaker: Maren
session_10.text: Ha, the sad sandwich is part of the ritual. I should get out more like that. I mostly just drag myself to the gym these days, I've got a membership at the Ironbridge gym and I'm weirdly loyal to it.

session_10.speaker: Isak
session_10.text: Weirdly loyal is the good kind. Better than paying for something and never going.

session_10.speaker: Maren
session_10.text: True. Anyway, the reason I'm sleeping badly is my upstairs neighbour. Somebody there drags furniture around at midnight.

session_10.speaker: Isak
session_10.text: Midnight furniture rearranging is a crime. Have you said anything to them?

session_10.speaker: Maren
session_10.text: Not yet. I keep hoping it'll stop on its own, but I think I'm going to have to leave a polite note.

session_10.speaker: Isak
session_10.text: Polite note first, then escalate to passive aggressive baking. Works every time.

session_10.speaker: Maren
session_10.text: Ha, I'll keep that in my back pocket. Okay, change of subject, I need something to look forward to. Have you thought about a holiday this year?

session_10.speaker: Isak
session_10.text: A bit. I'm leaning toward somewhere cooler, maybe mountains and lakes, nothing too busy.

session_10.speaker: Maren
session_10.text: That sounds perfect. I'd want a mix, a few lazy days and then one proper adventure so I don't feel like I wasted it.

session_10.speaker: Isak
session_10.text: Same. Lazy days with one adventure sprinkled in is the ideal ratio.

session_10.speaker: Maren
session_10.text: Right? Let's compare ideas next time we chat. I'll do some actual research this week.

session_10.speaker: Isak
session_10.text: Deal. Go get some sleep, and good luck with the furniture person.

session_11.speaker: Maren
session_11.text: Hey you! Finally sitting down with a coffee after a very long Monday. How's your week starting?

session_11.speaker: Isak
session_11.text: Slow and pleasant, honestly. I've been listening to this podcast about lost shipwrecks on my walks, and I'm weirdly hooked.

session_11.speaker: Maren
session_11.text: Ha, that sounds right up your street. Is it one of those with dramatic music and a hushed narrator?

session_11.speaker: Isak
session_11.text: Exactly that. The narrator whispers like he's afraid of waking the ship up.

session_11.speaker: Maren
session_11.text: Work news, by the way, I don't think I told you properly. I'm at Tallow & Pine now, and so far it feels like a much better fit.

session_11.speaker: Isak
session_11.text: Oh nice, that's good to hear! You sounded pretty ready for a change.

session_11.speaker: Maren
session_11.text: I was. Everyone's been welcoming, and nobody has scheduled a meeting that could have been an email yet.

session_11.speaker: Isak
session_11.text: Give it a month. Anyway, are we still on for book club this week? I'm planning to head to Marginalia straight after work, it's been our spot all along.

session_11.speaker: Maren
session_11.text: I'll try, depends how the week shapes up. I watched a film last night, though, an old black and white thing my neighbour recommended.

session_11.speaker: Isak
session_11.text: Oh? Was it any good, or one of those where you stay loyal out of politeness?

session_11.speaker: Maren
session_11.text: Properly good, actually. Slow, but the ending stuck with me for hours afterwards.

session_11.speaker: Isak
session_11.text: Those are the best kind. I need something like that, I've been rewatching comfort shows far too much lately.

session_11.speaker: Maren
session_11.text: Nothing wrong with comfort shows. Oh, and I picked up a new plant at the weekend, the jade plant. It's sitting on my windowsill looking smug.

session_11.speaker: Isak
session_11.text: Smug is the right word for jade plants. Let's hope it survives your enthusiasm.

session_11.speaker: Maren
session_11.text: Rude, but fair. Have you thought about any holiday plans? I'm craving somewhere with water and no schedule.

session_11.speaker: Isak
session_11.text: Same. Somewhere coastal and quiet, with a book and nothing to be on time for. I'd happily do that for a week.

session_11.speaker: Maren
session_11.text: That's the dream. Let's compare notes next time and maybe actually commit to something.

session_12.speaker: Maren
session_12.text: Okay, I need to tell you about the disaster I made last night. I tried a new braised chicken recipe and somehow ended up with something closer to chicken soup with a crust on top.

session_12.speaker: Isak
session_12.text: Ha, how does that even happen? Did you forget to put the lid on or something?

session_12.speaker: Maren
session_12.text: I think I did the opposite. The recipe said to cover it for the whole hour and I'm pretty sure it needed the lid off for the last twenty minutes. Lesson learned, I guess.

session_12.speaker: Isak
session_12.text: I once made a risotto that came out like wallpaper paste. Cooking is basically just a series of small humiliations.

session_12.speaker: Maren
session_12.text: Wallpaper paste, that's vivid. At least mine was edible, just very sad looking. I ate it standing at the counter like it was a secret.

session_12.speaker: Isak
session_12.text: Honestly the best way to eat a failed dinner. Anyway, have you listened to anything good lately? I've been stuck on a podcast about abandoned railway lines and I can't stop.

session_12.speaker: Maren
session_12.text: That sounds weirdly right up my alley. I've been working through one about the history of everyday objects, like the zipper and the paperclip. Sounds dull, it's actually really funny.

session_12.speaker: Isak
session_12.text: Okay, now I'm adding that to my list. The railway one has this host who gets way too emotional about old signal boxes, which is why I love it.

session_12.speaker: Maren
session_12.text: Emotional about signal boxes is the energy I want in a podcast host. Do you listen while you walk, or just at home?

session_12.speaker: Isak
session_12.text: Mostly while I'm out walking, actually. I finally did that ridge trail I kept talking about last weekend, the one with the long climb at the start.

session_12.speaker: Maren
session_12.text: Oh nice, how was it? I remember you saying the first stretch was supposed to be brutal.

session_12.speaker: Isak
session_12.text: Brutal but worth it. The view from the top was ridiculous, you could see all the way across the valley, and there was hardly anyone else up there.

session_12.speaker: Maren
session_12.text: Now I'm jealous. I haven't been properly hiking in ages, I keep saying I'll go and then the weekend disappears.

session_12.speaker: Isak
session_12.text: You should come next time, it's not too steep once you're past the first bit. I'll even bring snacks so you don't have to cook anything.

session_12.speaker: Maren
session_12.text: Deal, as long as the snacks aren't another one of your experimental trail mixes. The last one had something in it I still can't identify.

session_12.speaker: Isak
session_12.text: That was dried pear, it's a classic! Fine, I'll keep it simple. Let's pick a weekend soon.

session_13.speaker: Maren
session_13.text: Hey Isak! Finally sitting down for a proper chat. How's your week been?

session_13.speaker: Isak
session_13.text: Pretty decent, just slow. I've been listening to that podcast about lost expeditions on my walks, it's weirdly gripping.

session_13.speaker: Maren
session_13.text: Oh nice, is that the one with the two hosts who keep arguing about maps? I started it last week and got hooked on the second episode.

session_13.speaker: Isak
session_13.text: Yes, that one! The arguing is half the charm. What's new with you, anything happening?

session_13.speaker: Maren
session_13.text: Actually yes, big news on the work front. I switched jobs and I'm at Corvid Analytics now, started a couple of weeks ago.

session_13.speaker: Isak
session_13.text: Congrats, that's a big move! How are the first weeks treating you?

session_13.speaker: Maren
session_13.text: Good so far, people are friendly. Also I finally changed dentists, I'm seeing Dr. Yoon now and the office is so much calmer than my old one.

session_13.speaker: Isak
session_13.text: A calm dentist is a rare find, hang onto that. Are you settled in otherwise?

session_13.speaker: Maren
session_13.text: Mostly, yes. I'm in Graz and still figuring out which bakery is my favourite.

session_13.speaker: Isak
session_13.text: Ha, a worthy quest. Any plans for the weekend, or is the weather going to decide for you?

session_13.speaker: Maren
session_13.text: Oops, correction, I typed the wrong city a second ago. It's Dunedin, not Graz, my brain is clearly still on a different track today.

session_13.speaker: Isak
session_13.text: Ha, no worries, that happens. Anyway, the forecast here says rain on Saturday and sun on Sunday, so I'm planning a long walk on Sunday.

session_13.speaker: Maren
session_13.text: Same pattern here, grey Saturday, then it clears up. I might go for a coastal walk and finish the podcast, and I'm paying $38 a month for my phone now so at least I can stream it without worrying.

session_13.speaker: Isak
session_13.text: Perfect plan. Meanwhile my upstairs neighbour has started moving furniture around at eleven at night, I swear he rearranges his flat daily.

session_13.speaker: Maren
session_13.text: Oh no, that's the worst. Have you tried leaving a friendly note? Sometimes people honestly have no idea how much it carries.

session_13.speaker: Isak
session_13.text: I might do that before I lose it entirely. Anyway, talk again in a couple of weeks, enjoy your walk!

session_14.speaker: Maren
session_14.text: Okay, I finally have news on the wedding front. Did you get the invite from Tobias and Lena too?

session_14.speaker: Isak
session_14.text: Yes! It landed on my doormat on Saturday, with a little pressed flower tucked inside. Very fancy.

session_14.speaker: Maren
session_14.text: Ha, ours had one too. I'm already stressing about what to wear, since they said 'garden formal', whatever that means.

session_14.speaker: Isak
session_14.text: I think it means don't wear heels you'll sink into the lawn with. I'm planning on a linen jacket and hoping for the best.

session_14.speaker: Maren
session_14.text: Smart. Honestly I'm more excited about the day after, when everyone's hungover and we all end up at some greasy café.

session_14.speaker: Isak
session_14.text: That's the real highlight of any wedding. Speaking of food, I tried making a risotto last night and it was a disaster.

session_14.speaker: Maren
session_14.text: Oh no, what happened? Risotto is one of those things that looks easy and then isn't.

session_14.speaker: Isak
session_14.text: I got distracted answering a message and the bottom scorched, then I panicked and added way too much stock. It ended up somewhere between soup and porridge.

session_14.speaker: Maren
session_14.text: Soup-porridge, the forbidden dish. Did you eat it anyway?

session_14.speaker: Isak
session_14.text: I did, with a lot of cheese on top. Cheese covers a multitude of sins.

session_14.speaker: Maren
session_14.text: Truly. Anyway, I've been daydreaming about a trip lately, maybe somewhere with a coast and not much to do except wander around.

session_14.speaker: Isak
session_14.text: That sounds perfect. I keep thinking about going somewhere quiet in the off-season, when the crowds have gone home.

session_14.speaker: Maren
session_14.text: Yes, exactly that. Cold sea air, a big jumper, long lunches. I'd take that over a beach any day.

session_14.speaker: Isak
session_14.text: We should actually plan something instead of just talking about it for another year.

session_14.speaker: Maren
session_14.text: Deal. Let's pick a rough direction after the wedding, once the outfit crisis is over.

session_14.speaker: Isak
session_14.text: Sounds good. And I'll practise the risotto again so I can redeem myself.

session_15.speaker: Maren
session_15.text: Okay, I have to tell you about the film I watched last night. It was supposed to be a quiet little drama and it turned into a two-hour stare at a man fixing a boat.

session_15.speaker: Isak
session_15.text: Ha, I think I know the one. Was the boat a metaphor or just a boat?

session_15.speaker: Maren
session_15.text: Honestly I couldn't tell. Someone behind me in the cinema sighed so loudly at the end that I almost clapped.

session_15.speaker: Isak
session_15.text: Brutal. I watched something much dumber on Friday, a heist thing where everyone wears sunglasses indoors. Loved every minute.

session_15.speaker: Maren
session_15.text: Sometimes that's exactly what you need. Did you get the invite for Tomas and Elin's wedding, by the way?

session_15.speaker: Isak
session_15.text: Yes! Finally someone in our circle is doing it properly, with a long weekend and everything. I'm already worried about the speeches.

session_15.speaker: Maren
session_15.text: Tomas said he's writing his own vows and refuses to show anyone. That's either going to be beautiful or a disaster.

session_15.speaker: Isak
session_15.text: Knowing him, both at once. I'll bring tissues and a straight face.

session_15.speaker: Maren
session_15.text: Smart. Oh, I tried making that braised cabbage recipe you sent me and it went sideways.

session_15.speaker: Isak
session_15.text: Oh no, what happened? That one is nearly impossible to ruin.

session_15.speaker: Maren
session_15.text: I turned the heat up to speed it along and ended up with something between charcoal and soup. The whole flat smelled like a campfire for a day.

session_15.speaker: Isak
session_15.text: Okay, that's impressive, I'll give you that. The trick is patience, it really does want low and slow.

session_15.speaker: Maren
session_15.text: Lesson learned. I ordered a pizza and called it a night.

session_15.speaker: Isak
session_15.text: Honestly the correct decision. I once set off the smoke alarm making toast, so I'm not judging.

session_15.speaker: Maren
session_15.text: Toast is a bold way to go out. Let's talk in two weeks, and send me a better recipe by then, one with fewer ways to fail.

session_15.speaker: Isak
session_15.text: Deal. I'll find you something foolproof, or at least fool-resistant.

session_16.speaker: Isak
session_16.text: Hey you! Finally got a quiet evening, so I thought I'd catch up properly. How's your week been?

session_16.speaker: Maren
session_16.text: Pretty calm, honestly. I watched a film on Tuesday night that I'd been meaning to see for ages, that slow Norwegian one about the lighthouse keeper.

session_16.speaker: Isak
session_16.text: Oh, the one with the long silent stretches? I tried watching that and fell asleep twenty minutes in. Was it worth sticking with?

session_16.speaker: Maren
session_16.text: Ha, yes, it's very much a fall-asleep film at the start. But the ending got me. The last half hour is gorgeous, all fog and gulls and this one huge storm scene.

session_16.speaker: Isak
session_16.text: Okay, I'll give it another go then. Maybe not right before bed this time.

session_16.speaker: Maren
session_16.text: Definitely not. Afternoon with a big mug of tea is the way to do it.

session_16.speaker: Isak
session_16.text: Noted. Hey, did you ever do that ridge trail you were talking about? The one with the stone hut at the top?

session_16.speaker: Maren
session_16.text: Not yet! I keep eyeing it but every time I plan it, the forecast turns grim. I read that the last stretch gets really slippery when it's wet.

session_16.speaker: Isak
session_16.text: Yeah, I did it years ago and the final scramble is no joke in the rain. Worth it for the view though, you can see all the way down the valley on a clear day.

session_16.speaker: Maren
session_16.text: That's exactly the view I want. Speaking of which, do you know what the weather's doing this weekend? I haven't looked yet.

session_16.speaker: Isak
session_16.text: I glanced earlier and it looked decent. Cold and bright on Saturday, then clouds rolling in on Sunday with maybe some drizzle.

session_16.speaker: Maren
session_16.text: Cold and bright is perfect hiking weather. Saturday morning might finally be the day for that ridge.

session_16.speaker: Isak
session_16.text: Do it! Start early, take a flask, and bring gloves because the wind up top is brutal this time of year.

session_16.speaker: Maren
session_16.text: Good tip, I'd have forgotten the gloves for sure. I'll send you a photo from the hut if I make it.

session_16.speaker: Isak
session_16.text: Please do. And I'll report back on whether I survive the lighthouse film in the afternoon.

session_16.speaker: Maren
session_16.text: Deal. Talk in a couple of weeks, and good luck staying awake!

session_1.speaker: Dalia
session_1.text: Happy new year, Corwin! Did you get any real time off, or were you checking Slack the whole break?

session_1.speaker: Corwin
session_1.text: Happy new year! I tried to stay away and mostly managed. Only peeked twice, which for me is basically a vacation.

session_1.speaker: Dalia
session_1.text: Respect. I came back to find the office coffee machine making a horrible grinding noise. Sounds like a blender full of gravel.

session_1.speaker: Corwin
session_1.text: Oh no, I heard about that. Somebody taped a sign on it that just says 'be gentle.' I don't think that's a maintenance plan.

session_1.speaker: Dalia
session_1.text: Ha, no. I've started going to the little cafe downstairs instead. It's a bit pricey but at least it doesn't scream at me.

session_1.speaker: Corwin
session_1.text: Fair. I'll probably join you if it's not fixed by Wednesday.

session_1.speaker: Dalia
session_1.text: Deal. On a less fun note, I spent part of this morning chasing a flaky test. It passes, it fails, it passes again, no changes in between.

session_1.speaker: Corwin
session_1.text: Ugh, the worst kind. Is it a timing thing, you think?

session_1.speaker: Dalia
session_1.text: Probably something like that. I'll poke at it more tomorrow, but I'm not hopeful it's a quick fix.

session_1.speaker: Corwin
session_1.text: Well, don't sink the whole week into it. If it's truly random, maybe we quarantine it and note it down so it doesn't get forgotten.

session_1.speaker: Dalia
session_1.text: That's reasonable. Noting things down is a whole other problem though. Our documentation is in rough shape.

session_1.speaker: Corwin
session_1.text: Don't remind me. Half the setup guides still describe how things worked a long time ago. I keep meaning to block out time for it.

session_1.speaker: Dalia
session_1.text: Same. I rewrote one page before the holidays and it felt great, like cleaning out a closet. Then I looked at how many other pages there are and felt less great.

session_1.speaker: Corwin
session_1.text: Maybe we pick one page each sprint and just chip away. Small and steady beats a big heroic cleanup that never happens.

session_1.speaker: Dalia
session_1.text: I like that. Low pressure, and we actually might stick to it.

session_1.speaker: Corwin
session_1.text: Great, I'll add it to the agenda for our next planning meeting. Talk in a couple of weeks, and good luck with that test!

session_2.speaker: Dalia
session_2.text: Hey Corwin, finally got my new laptop set up yesterday. The old one was wheezing every time I opened more than three browser tabs.

session_2.speaker: Corwin
session_2.text: Ha, about time. How is it? Fast enough that you'll stop complaining?

session_2.speaker: Dalia
session_2.text: Night and day, honestly. Full builds that used to make me go get coffee now finish before I've stood up.

session_2.speaker: Corwin
session_2.text: Nice. Did you have to reinstall everything from scratch or did the migration tool do its thing?

session_2.speaker: Dalia
session_2.text: Mostly a fresh install, I wanted to clean out years of junk. Took an afternoon but it felt good.

session_2.speaker: Corwin
session_2.text: Fair enough. Anything weird come up while you were getting the toolchain working again?

session_2.speaker: Dalia
session_2.text: Only when I was checking that our pipeline still ran from my machine. Everything we build goes through CircleCI, so I just pushed a tiny branch and watched it go green.

session_2.speaker: Corwin
session_2.text: Good, that's the best kind of smoke test. Speaking of green, is that one flaky test still giving people grief?

session_2.speaker: Dalia
session_2.text: Yeah, it passes nine times and then randomly fails on the tenth. I suspect it's a timing thing, but I haven't had a chance to dig in properly.

session_2.speaker: Corwin
session_2.text: Those are the worst. People start re-running instead of investigating and then nobody trusts the suite.

session_2.speaker: Dalia
session_2.text: Exactly. I'd rather quarantine it and fix it for real than keep hitting retry and hoping.

session_2.speaker: Corwin
session_2.text: Agreed. Different topic, I've been meaning to ask how code review has been feeling lately. I saw a couple of pretty blunt comments go by this week.

session_2.speaker: Dalia
session_2.text: Yeah, I noticed. I think people forget tone doesn't carry well in text, so a short comment reads colder than intended.

session_2.speaker: Corwin
session_2.text: Right. I'd love it if we leaned toward asking questions instead of issuing verdicts, like 'what do you think about trying this' rather than 'this is wrong'.

session_2.speaker: Dalia
session_2.text: That's my approach too. And mentioning something that's done well in the diff costs nothing and makes the rest easier to hear.

session_2.speaker: Corwin
session_2.text: Couldn't have said it better. Maybe I'll drop a short note about it in the team channel without calling anyone out.

session_2.speaker: Dalia
session_2.text: Sounds good. Talk in a couple of weeks, enjoy the rest of your week!

session_3.speaker: Corwin
session_3.text: Hey Dalia, how's the week treating you? I feel like I've been in meetings since Monday.

session_3.speaker: Dalia
session_3.text: Same here, honestly. Mostly heads-down on reviews today, which is a nice change.

session_3.speaker: Corwin
session_3.text: Oh nice. Anything interesting in the review queue?

session_3.speaker: Dalia
session_3.text: One PR where the comments got a bit spicy. I keep trying to phrase feedback as questions instead of orders, like 'what do you think about splitting this out?' It lands so much better.

session_3.speaker: Corwin
session_3.text: That's a good habit. I've noticed people respond way better when the tone is curious rather than corrective.

session_3.speaker: Dalia
session_3.text: Right, and speaking of things landing badly: a new blocker bug was opened on the release today, the duplicate invoice bug. I'm going to dig into it this afternoon.

session_3.speaker: Corwin
session_3.text: Ugh, okay, thanks for the heads up. Let me know if you need anything from me to clear the path.

session_3.speaker: Dalia
session_3.text: Will do. Mostly I just need uninterrupted time, so maybe keep the pings light for a bit.

session_3.speaker: Corwin
session_3.text: Deal. Changing the subject slightly, I realized our documentation is way behind. Half the setup notes still describe how things worked months ago.

session_3.speaker: Dalia
session_3.text: Yeah, the docs debt is real. Every time I onboard someone I end up correcting the README out loud instead of fixing it.

session_3.speaker: Corwin
session_3.text: Maybe we carve out an hour every Friday just for docs? Nothing heroic, just chipping away.

session_3.speaker: Dalia
session_3.text: I'd be into that. Small and regular beats a giant cleanup sprint that never happens.

session_3.speaker: Corwin
session_3.text: Agreed. Oh, and the team lunch is set for next Thursday, by the way. I was thinking that noodle place near the office.

session_3.speaker: Dalia
session_3.text: Yes please, I've been wanting their spicy noodles forever. Is everyone coming in person?

session_3.speaker: Corwin
session_3.text: Most people, I think. I'll send a quick poll so we can lock in a table.

session_3.speaker: Dalia
session_3.text: Perfect. Okay, I'm going to get back to my review pile. Talk soon!

session_4.speaker: Corwin
session_4.text: Hey Dalia, did you get a chance to watch any of the talks from the conference last week? I heard the keynote was a bit of a snooze.

session_4.speaker: Dalia
session_4.text: I caught the one on incremental builds and it was actually great. The speaker had a funny way of walking through a failed experiment, which made it stick.

session_4.speaker: Corwin
session_4.text: Ha, I love when people admit what didn't work. Way more useful than a polished success story.

session_4.speaker: Dalia
session_4.text: Totally. Meanwhile the coffee machine on our floor is making a grinding noise again. I think it's begging for mercy.

session_4.speaker: Corwin
session_4.text: Oh no, not again. I'll ping facilities, though last time they just descaled it and called it a day.

session_4.speaker: Dalia
session_4.text: Descaling is fine, but I'd honestly settle for it just not sounding like a cement mixer at 9am.

session_4.speaker: Corwin
session_4.text: Fair. Speaking of small annoyances, I've noticed some review comments lately that feel a bit curt. Nothing from you, just in general.

session_4.speaker: Dalia
session_4.text: Yeah, I've seen that too. Text strips out tone, so a plain 'why is this here' can land way harder than someone intended.

session_4.speaker: Corwin
session_4.text: Right. I'd love to nudge people toward asking questions instead of making demands, something like 'what was the thinking here?'

session_4.speaker: Dalia
session_4.text: I like that. I also try to say what's good in a PR before I pick at anything, even if it's just one line.

session_4.speaker: Corwin
session_4.text: That's a good habit. Maybe I'll float it at the next team sync as a soft guideline rather than a rule.

session_4.speaker: Dalia
session_4.text: Soft is the way to go. Nobody likes a rulebook about being nice, it just makes people self-conscious.

session_4.speaker: Corwin
session_4.text: Ha, true. Okay, I should run, I've got a meeting starting in a few minutes.

session_4.speaker: Dalia
session_4.text: No worries. Let me know what facilities says about the coffee machine, I might bring my own beans in the meantime.

session_4.speaker: Corwin
session_4.text: Will do. If the grinder dies for good I'm blaming you for jinxing it.

session_4.speaker: Dalia
session_4.text: Deal. Talk soon!

session_5.speaker: Corwin
session_5.text: Hey Dalia, how's your week been? I feel like I've been in meetings nonstop.

session_5.speaker: Dalia
session_5.text: Pretty good overall, apart from one test that keeps failing randomly. It passes on my machine, then fails for no reason an hour later.

session_5.speaker: Corwin
session_5.text: Ugh, flaky tests are the worst. Do you have any idea what's causing it?

session_5.speaker: Dalia
session_5.text: Probably some timing assumption. Oh, and by the way, we're running everything on SQLite, which is part of why the local setup is so easy to spin up.

session_5.speaker: Corwin
session_5.text: Good to know, that makes sense for keeping things simple. Did you catch that conference talk I sent around?

session_5.speaker: Dalia
session_5.text: I watched half of it last night. The speaker's section on keeping feedback loops short was actually really useful.

session_5.speaker: Corwin
session_5.text: Yeah, that was my favorite part too. I might try pitching a smaller version of that idea to the team.

session_5.speaker: Dalia
session_5.text: Do it. Also, since you asked about infra the other day, the service is hosted in Singapore, so latency for us is fine but a bit slower for folks elsewhere.

session_5.speaker: Corwin
session_5.text: Got it, thanks. I'll pass that along if anyone asks.

session_5.speaker: Dalia
session_5.text: Speaking of the team, I've been trying to be better about code review manners. I used to just write 'fix this' and now I try to explain why.

session_5.speaker: Corwin
session_5.text: Honestly that goes a long way. People take suggestions way better when there's a reason attached.

session_5.speaker: Dalia
session_5.text: Right? Oh, before I forget, Priya owns the billing module, so any questions on that should go to her.

session_5.speaker: Corwin
session_5.text: Perfect, I'll loop her in on the thread then. Thanks for the heads up.

session_5.speaker: Dalia
session_5.text: No problem. One more thing, a new blocker bug was just opened on the release: the timezone drift.

session_5.speaker: Corwin

session_6.speaker: Corwin
session_6.text: How's the newcomer doing, by the way? I saw she opened her first pull request yesterday.

session_6.text: She's settling in well. Asks good questions and doesn't get flustered when the build does something weird. Her first PR was tidy, just a couple of small naming nits.

session_6.text: Great. Speaking of PRs, I've been thinking about review manners lately. Some comments on our team read a bit sharp.

session_6.speaker: Corwin
session_6.text: Ah, okay, good to know. I'll fix my notes. And yes, I like the question approach for reviews, it keeps people from getting defensive.

session_6.speaker: Dalia
session_6.text: Also, to be clear for anyone wondering, Anselm leads design on the project. That's settled.

session_6.speaker: Corwin
session_6.text: Understood. Back to the newcomer for a sec: do you think she'd benefit from a short walkthrough of how we do reviews?

session_6.speaker: Dalia
session_6.text: Definitely. A short doc plus a quick call would do it, and I can sit in on her next couple of reviews so she sees the tone we aim for.

session_6.speaker: Corwin
session_6.text: Perfect, that works for me. Enjoy the new laptop, and let me know if the fans ever get loud.

session_6.speaker: Dalia
session_6.text: Will do. Talk in a couple of weeks!

session_7.speaker: Corwin
session_7.text: Morning! Did you see the coffee machine finally got descaled? First cup in weeks that didn't taste like a pencil.

session_7.speaker: Dalia
session_7.text: Ha, I noticed. Somebody finally filed the ticket, apparently. I'm on my second cup and still feeling human.

session_7.text: Good. So, quick heads up before I forget: we've moved the builds over, and the project now runs on Jenkins.

session_7.speaker: Dalia

session_7.text: How's the new hire settling in, by the way? I saw you walking her through the setup yesterday.

session_7.text: Fingers crossed. Did you catch that conference talk everyone's been sharing? The one about small teams shipping faster.

session_8.speaker: Corwin
session_8.text: Morning! Did you see the coffee machine is finally fixed? Someone left a note saying it now makes 'actual espresso'.

session_8.speaker: Dalia
session_8.text: I saw. I'm skeptical, but I had a cup an hour ago and it was decent, so maybe there's hope.

session_8.speaker: Corwin
session_8.text: Good news. How's the laptop upgrade going, by the way? IT said yours was scheduled this week.

session_8.speaker: Dalia
session_8.text: It arrived yesterday. Setup is mostly done, though I'm still reinstalling tools. Oh, and we've moved our pipelines over, so the CI system we build on is Buildkite now.

session_8.speaker: Corwin
session_8.text: Nice, that should simplify things. Is the new machine noticeably faster?

session_8.speaker: Dalia
session_8.text: Way faster. Builds that used to make me go refill my coffee now finish before I stand up.

session_8.speaker: Corwin
session_8.text: Ha, which is bad for your coffee habit. Speaking of spending, I'm filling in the finance form. What's our quarterly cloud budget again?

session_8.speaker: Dalia
session_8.text: I believe it's $31,000 for the quarter.

session_8.speaker: Corwin
session_8.text: Okay, I'll put that down. Give me a second, I'm typing it in.

session_8.speaker: Dalia
session_8.text: Wait, hold on, I got that wrong, sorry. It's not $31,000, that was a mistake on my part. The quarterly cloud budget is $24,500.

session_8.speaker: Corwin
session_8.text: Good catch, fixing it now. Better to sort that out before finance sees it.

session_8.speaker: Dalia
session_8.text: Agreed. Anyway, I'll look over the invoice questions tomorrow, and Henrik handles billing module stuff now, so I'll loop him in on any of the code side.

session_8.speaker: Corwin
session_8.text: Sounds good. Are you joining the team lunch on Friday? I think we're trying that new noodle place.

session_8.speaker: Dalia
session_8.text: Definitely. Though I should warn you, QA just opened a new blocker on the release: the export crash.

session_8.speaker: Corwin
session_8.text: Ugh, okay. Let's talk it through after lunch, then, so it doesn't spoil the noodles.

session_8.speaker: Dalia
session_8.text: Fair. I'll start digging into it in the repo, kestrel-core, this afternoon so I have something to show you.

session_8.speaker: Corwin
session_8.text: Perfect. Enjoy the new laptop and the fancy espresso in the meantime.

session_9.speaker: Dalia
session_9.text: Hey Corwin, how's your Monday going? Mine started with way too much coffee.

session_9.speaker: Corwin
session_9.text: Ha, same here. Busy but good. Did you get a chance to meet the new person who started last week?

session_9.speaker: Dalia
session_9.text: Yeah, we paired for a bit on Friday. Sharp, asks good questions, and already figured out how to run everything locally.

session_9.speaker: Corwin
session_9.text: Great, I was hoping they'd settle in quickly. I'll check in with them later this week so they don't feel lost.

session_9.speaker: Dalia
session_9.text: Good idea. Oh, and before I forget, the duplicate invoice bug is fixed and closed. It merged this morning and nothing weird showed up after.

session_9.speaker: Corwin
session_9.text: Nice, that's a relief. Thanks for chasing it down.

session_9.speaker: Dalia
session_9.text: No problem. The newcomer actually left a really polite review comment on my patch, which made me think about review manners in general.

session_9.speaker: Corwin
session_9.text: Oh yeah? I'm a big believer in phrasing things as questions rather than orders. 'What do you think about trying X?' lands way better than 'change this'.

session_9.text: Totally. And praising the stuff that's actually good, not just pointing out what's wrong. People forget that part.

session_9.speaker: Corwin
session_9.text: Agreed. Also no nitpicking on style when a linter could handle it. Saves everyone's patience.

session_9.speaker: Dalia
session_9.text: Ha, yes. Speaking of tools, I finally got approval to upgrade my laptop. The old one sounds like a jet engine whenever I compile anything.

session_9.speaker: Corwin
session_9.text: Finally! What are you getting? I've been eyeing a lighter one for my commute.

session_9.speaker: Dalia
session_9.text: Something with a lot more memory and a better battery. I'm mostly excited about not having to carry the charger everywhere.

session_9.speaker: Corwin
session_9.text: That alone is worth it. Let me know how it feels once it arrives, I might copy your choice.

session_9.speaker: Dalia
session_9.text: Will do. Setting it up will probably eat a whole afternoon though.

session_9.speaker: Corwin
session_9.text: Worth it. Alright, I'll let you get back to it. Talk in a couple of weeks!

session_10.speaker: Dalia
session_10.text: Morning! Fair warning, I'm typing this on the new laptop and the keyboard feels completely different. I keep hitting the wrong keys.

session_10.speaker: Corwin
session_10.text: Ha, the upgrade finally landed? How's it running compared to the old one?

session_10.text: Way faster. Builds that used to make me go get coffee now finish before I stand up. Migrating all my dotfiles was a pain though.

session_10.text: Worth it, I'd say. Anything on the Kestrel side I should know about this week?

session_10.text: Good to hear it was painless. I'll update the architecture overview so it doesn't say something stale.

session_10.speaker: Dalia
session_10.text: Speaking of docs, we really have a pile of documentation debt. Half the setup guide still describes how things worked ages ago.

session_10.speaker: Corwin
session_10.text: Yeah, I know, that one's on my conscience. Maybe we carve out a half day next sprint just for cleaning up docs?

session_10.speaker: Dalia
session_10.text: I'd be into that. Even just deleting the outdated pages would help a lot.

session_10.speaker: Corwin
session_10.text: Deal. How's the pre-release testing looking overall?

session_10.speaker: Dalia
session_10.text: Mostly on track. We do have a contract with Quillon for the load testing, so that side is covered and I don't have to build the harness myself.

session_10.speaker: Corwin
session_10.text: Nice, that saves you a ton of time. Anything nasty turn up?

session_10.speaker: Dalia
session_10.text: One thing, yes. A new blocker bug got opened on the release: the sync memory leak. I only started digging into it this morning.

session_10.speaker: Corwin
session_10.text: Okay, thanks for flagging it. Let me know if you need me to shuffle anyone's priorities to help.

session_10.speaker: Dalia
session_10.text: Will do. Also, there's this one flaky test that fails maybe one run in ten and nobody can pin down why. It's driving me up the wall.

session_10.speaker: Corwin
session_10.text: Classic. Flaky tests are the worst, they teach everyone to just hit rerun. Let's give it an hour of focused attention before it rots further.

session_11.speaker: Corwin
session_11.text: Hey Dalia, how's the new laptop treating you? I heard IT finally swapped yours out.

session_11.speaker: Dalia
session_11.text: Finally, yes! It showed up Monday and I've spent most of the week just getting my setup back to normal. The fans are way quieter though, so I'm not complaining.

session_11.speaker: Corwin
session_11.text: Nice. Mine is due for an upgrade too but I keep putting it off because I dread the migration part.

session_11.speaker: Dalia
session_11.text: Honestly, just write down your dotfiles and installed tools before you start. That saved me about half a day of confusion.

session_11.speaker: Corwin
session_11.text: Good tip, I'll do that. Also, are you coming to the team lunch on Friday? I'm trying to get a headcount.

session_11.speaker: Dalia
session_11.text: Yep, count me in. Is it still the noodle place down the street, or did people vote for something else?

session_11.speaker: Corwin
session_11.text: Still the noodle place. Someone suggested tacos but the noodle camp was louder.

session_11.speaker: Dalia
session_11.text: Ha, fair enough. I'm fine with noodles, as long as they have a decent vegetarian option.

session_11.speaker: Corwin
session_11.text: They do, I checked the menu last time. Totally unrelated, but I've been feeling guilty about our documentation lately. So much of it is out of date.

session_11.speaker: Dalia
session_11.text: Oh, tell me about it. I opened the setup guide last week and half the steps referenced things we stopped using ages ago.

session_11.speaker: Corwin
session_11.text: That's exactly the kind of thing I mean. New people hit it and lose a day just figuring out what's still real.

session_11.speaker: Dalia
session_11.text: Maybe we could set aside an afternoon, just a docs cleanup session where everyone fixes whatever page they touched last. Small and low pressure.

session_11.speaker: Corwin
session_11.text: I like that. Small and scoped is the only way it'll actually happen. I'll try to find a slot that doesn't clash with anything.

session_11.speaker: Dalia
session_11.text: Maybe pair it with the lunch? Everyone's in a good mood after noodles, so they might be more willing.

session_11.speaker: Corwin
session_11.text: Ha, bribing people with food to write docs. Honestly, that might work better than any process I could come up with.

session_11.speaker: Dalia
session_11.text: Worked on me every time. Alright, I'll go finish unpacking my digital life onto this laptop, talk soon!

session_12.speaker: Corwin
session_12.text: Hey Dalia, got a minute? I wanted to ask how your week has been going.

session_12.speaker: Dalia
session_12.text: Pretty decent, actually. Spent a good chunk of it reviewing other people's pull requests, which got me thinking about review manners.

session_12.speaker: Corwin
session_12.text: Oh, I'd love to hear this. What's your take?

session_12.speaker: Dalia
session_12.text: Mostly that comments should be phrased as questions or suggestions, not commands. 'What do you think about extracting this?' lands way better than 'extract this.'

session_12.speaker: Corwin
session_12.text: That makes sense. I've seen reviews that read like a scolding and the author just goes quiet for two days.

session_12.speaker: Dalia
session_12.text: Right, and then the whole thing stalls. I also try to leave at least one genuine compliment if something's clever, otherwise it feels like a list of complaints.

session_12.speaker: Corwin
session_12.text: Good habit. Totally unrelated, but I watched a conference talk last night about running engineering teams with less meeting overhead.

session_12.speaker: Dalia
session_12.text: Ooh, was it any good? Those talks tend to be either super practical or just vibes.

session_12.speaker: Corwin
session_12.text: Surprisingly practical. The speaker's big idea was that every recurring meeting should have to re-justify itself every quarter, or it gets cancelled by default.

session_12.speaker: Dalia
session_12.text: I like that. Most standing meetings survive purely out of inertia.

session_12.speaker: Corwin
session_12.text: Exactly. I'm tempted to try it on my own calendar and see what's left.

session_12.speaker: Dalia
session_12.text: Let me know how brave you get. Meanwhile I've been fighting a flaky test that fails maybe one run in twenty, and only when the machine is under load.

session_12.speaker: Corwin
session_12.text: Ugh, those are the worst. Is it a timing thing?

session_12.speaker: Dalia
session_12.text: Almost certainly. Something is assuming an operation finishes within a fixed window, and when things get slow it just loses the race.

session_12.speaker: Corwin
session_12.text: Classic. Do you retry it or hunt down the real cause?

session_12.speaker: Dalia
session_12.text: Hunt it down. Retrying just hides the problem and teaches everyone to ignore red builds, which is how real failures slip through.

session_13.speaker: Corwin
session_13.text: Hey Dalia, how's your week going? Mine's been mostly meetings, so I'm a bit fried.

session_13.speaker: Dalia
session_13.text: Pretty good actually. The new hire started Monday and I've been helping her get her laptop and environment sorted.

session_13.speaker: Corwin
session_13.text: Oh nice, how's she settling in? I only met her briefly on the intro call.

session_13.speaker: Dalia
session_13.text: She's sharp and asks good questions, which I love. She's a bit shy in the team channel still, but that usually passes after a week or two.

session_13.speaker: Corwin
session_13.text: Good to hear. Did she get her first pull request up yet?

session_13.speaker: Dalia
session_13.text: Yeah, a small one yesterday, just a typo fix in a config file. I figured that's the gentlest way to learn how our review flow works.

session_13.speaker: Corwin
session_13.text: Smart. How did the review go? I always worry newcomers get steamrolled by overly picky comments.

session_13.speaker: Dalia
session_13.text: That's exactly what I tried to avoid. I told the reviewers to lead with what's good, phrase suggestions as questions, and not bury her in nitpicks on a first PR.

session_13.speaker: Corwin
session_13.text: Love that. I've seen people leave teams over a harsh review thread, so a little kindness goes a long way.

session_13.speaker: Dalia
session_13.text: Agreed. Honestly the rest of us could stand to be nicer in reviews too, I've caught myself writing 'why would you do this' more than once.

session_13.speaker: Corwin
session_13.text: Ha, guilty as well. Maybe we jot down a few review guidelines somewhere so it's not just tribal knowledge.

session_13.speaker: Dalia
session_13.text: That ties into the documentation mess, honestly. She hit three places where the setup guide was just wrong or missing steps.

session_13.speaker: Corwin
session_13.text: Ugh, the docs debt keeps biting us. Is she willing to note down what tripped her up while it's fresh?

session_13.speaker: Dalia
session_13.text: She already started a list. Fresh eyes are the best docs audit you can get, so I told her to fix things as she goes.

session_13.speaker: Corwin
session_13.text: Perfect. Let's carve out a little time next sprint to clean up the worst pages, even if it's just an afternoon.

session_13.speaker: Dalia
session_13.text: Sounds good to me. I'll set up a short doc-cleanup session and invite her so she feels like part of it.

session_14.speaker: Corwin
session_14.text: Hey Dalia, got a minute? Wanted to ask how the review comments have been landing lately. Someone on the team told me a few of them felt a bit blunt.

session_14.speaker: Dalia
session_14.text: Yeah, I've heard that too. I think it's mostly tone in text, nobody means anything by it. I've started opening with what I liked before getting into the nitpicks.

session_14.speaker: Corwin
session_14.text: That seems like a good habit. I always think a question lands better than a command, like 'what if we tried this?' instead of 'change this.'

session_14.speaker: Dalia
session_14.text: Totally. Also I'm trying to stop leaving drive-by comments on PRs I don't have context for. If I'm not going to actually review it properly, I'd rather say so.

session_14.speaker: Corwin
session_14.text: Fair. Speaking of things that annoy people, is that flaky test still acting up?

session_14.speaker: Dalia
session_14.text: Yep, it passes three times and then fails on the fourth for no reason I can see. I suspect a timing thing, but I haven't had a clean block of time to dig in.

session_14.speaker: Corwin
session_14.text: Ugh, those are the worst. Should we just quarantine it for now so it stops crying wolf?

session_14.speaker: Dalia
session_14.text: Probably, as long as we leave a note and a ticket so it doesn't get forgotten. Quarantined tests have a way of becoming permanent.

session_14.speaker: Corwin
session_14.text: True. Oh, before I forget, I need to update the vendor list for the next status report. Anything changed on your side?

session_14.speaker: Dalia
session_14.text: One thing, we ended the contract with Quillon. It wrapped up cleanly, so there's nothing hanging over us there.

session_14.speaker: Corwin
session_14.text: Got it, thanks. I'll take them off the list.

session_14.speaker: Dalia
session_14.text: While we're on reports, can you make sure the summary mentions that Northwind Dairy is the main client? I noticed the last one was kind of vague about who we're building this for.

session_14.speaker: Corwin
session_14.text: Good call, I'll make that explicit. People skim those things, so clearer is better.

session_14.speaker: Dalia
session_14.text: Same energy as our docs, honestly. We have a pile of documentation debt, half the setup guide is out of date.

session_14.speaker: Corwin
session_14.text: I know, and every new person trips over it. Maybe we block out one afternoon a month just for docs?

session_14.speaker: Dalia
session_14.text: I'd be into that. Even small fixes help, like correcting a stale command when you spot it instead of just grumbling.

session_14.speaker: Corwin
session_14.text: Deal. I'll put a recurring slot on the calendar and we'll see if it sticks.

session_15.speaker: Corwin
session_15.text: Hey Dalia, how's your week going? Mine's been a blur of standups.

session_15.speaker: Dalia
session_15.text: Pretty decent, actually. I spent half of Tuesday chasing a flaky test that only fails on the second run, never the first.

session_15.speaker: Corwin
session_15.text: Ugh, those are the worst. Did you track down what was causing it?

session_15.speaker: Dalia
session_15.text: Mostly. It was leaning on some shared state that another test left behind. I isolated it, but I'm keeping an eye on it for a few days.

session_15.speaker: Corwin
session_15.text: Good call. Oh, and on the design front, just so you have it straight: Marisol leads design on Kestrel, and she has the whole time.

session_15.speaker: Dalia
session_15.text: Speaking of things I've been putting off, our docs are in rough shape. Half the setup guide still describes how things worked ages ago.

session_15.speaker: Corwin
session_15.text: Yeah, documentation debt is sneaky. Nobody notices until a new person tries to follow it.

session_15.speaker: Dalia
session_15.text: Exactly, and that's how I found out. I was walking the new engineer through it and we hit three dead ends in the first twenty minutes.

session_15.speaker: Corwin
session_15.text: How's the newcomer settling in otherwise? I've barely talked to them.

session_15.speaker: Dalia
session_15.text: Really well. Asks good questions, and doesn't pretend to understand when they don't, which I appreciate.

session_15.speaker: Corwin
session_15.text: That's a great sign. Maybe have them fix the docs as they go? Fresh eyes catch the stale bits fastest.

session_15.speaker: Dalia
session_15.text: I was already planning that. They've started a running list of everything that tripped them up.

session_15.speaker: Corwin
session_15.text: Perfect. Anything on your plate I should know about before the weekend?

session_15.speaker: Dalia
session_15.text: One thing: the timezone drift is fixed and closed. Merged it yesterday and the numbers have stayed clean since.

session_15.speaker: Corwin
session_15.text: Nice, that one's been nagging at everyone. Thanks for seeing it through.

session_15.speaker: Dalia
session_15.text: Happy to. Now I just need to get the flaky test fully behind me and carve out an hour for those docs.

session_15.speaker: Corwin
session_15.text: Sounds like a plan. Enjoy the rest of your week!

session_16.speaker: Dalia
session_16.text: Hey Corwin, I finally watched that conference talk you sent around. The one about keeping reviews small.

session_16.speaker: Corwin
session_16.text: Oh nice, what did you think? I thought the speaker was a bit intense but the content was solid.

session_16.speaker: Dalia
session_16.text: Same. The bit about reviewing the code and not the person stuck with me. I've been trying to phrase my comments as questions lately.

session_16.speaker: Corwin
session_16.text: That's a good habit. 'What happens if this is null?' lands way softer than 'you forgot a null check.'

session_16.speaker: Dalia
session_16.text: Right? And it actually gets better answers sometimes, because people explain their reasoning instead of getting defensive.

session_16.speaker: Corwin
session_16.text: I'd add that approving fast on tiny changes matters too. Nobody wants a one-line fix sitting for three days.

session_16.speaker: Dalia
session_16.text: Ha, true. Although I'll admit I've let a few small ones sit just because I was deep in something else.

session_16.speaker: Corwin
session_16.text: We all do it. Honestly a quick 'I'll look this afternoon' message helps more than silence.

session_16.speaker: Dalia
session_16.text: Good call. Oh, unrelated, I spent half my morning chasing a flaky test. Passes nine times, fails on the tenth.

session_16.speaker: Corwin
session_16.text: Ugh, the worst kind. Is it usually timing, or something with shared state?

session_16.speaker: Dalia
session_16.text: Looks like timing. Something assumes an async thing finishes before the assertion runs, and mostly it does.

session_16.speaker: Corwin
session_16.text: Classic. Mostly works is the most dangerous phrase in testing.

session_16.speaker: Dalia
session_16.text: Agreed. I'm going to rewrite it to wait on the actual condition instead of sleeping for a fixed bit.

session_16.speaker: Corwin
session_16.text: Yes, please. Fixed sleeps are just flakiness with extra steps.

session_16.speaker: Dalia
session_16.text: Ha, I'm stealing that line for my next review comment. Phrased as a question, of course.

session_16.speaker: Corwin
session_16.text: Perfect. Talk again in a couple of weeks, enjoy the rest of your Sunday!
