session_1.speaker: Yusuf
session_1.text: Morning Petra, hope your week has started better than mine. Inbox is a disaster.

session_1.speaker: Petra
session_1.text: Morning! Same here, honestly. Took me an hour just to dig out from the weekend.

session_1.speaker: Yusuf
session_1.text: Have you heard anything from Marlow's side since we last spoke?

session_1.speaker: Petra
session_1.text: Not a word. They're taking days to answer even simple emails, it's getting a bit ridiculous.

session_1.speaker: Yusuf
session_1.text: Ha, that's about what I expected. They took nearly a week to confirm a meeting room last time.

session_1.speaker: Petra
session_1.text: I'll chase them again today. By the way, the liability cap is $2 million, just so you have that figure in front of you.

session_1.speaker: Yusuf
session_1.text: Okay, good to have it in writing. Thanks for flagging.

session_1.speaker: Petra
session_1.text: No problem. Should we pencil in another call for early next month?

session_1.speaker: Yusuf
session_1.text: Works for me. Mornings are better, I'm usually stuck in meetings after lunch.

session_1.speaker: Petra
session_1.text: Mornings it is. I'll send over a couple of slots later this week.

session_1.speaker: Yusuf
session_1.text: Perfect. Oh, my office is closed for the holiday on Monday, so I'll be offline that day.

session_1.speaker: Petra
session_1.text: Ours too, the whole firm shuts down. Nothing will move on my end until Tuesday.

session_1.speaker: Yusuf
session_1.text: Fine by me, it's not like Marlow will notice anyway given how slow they are.

session_1.speaker: Petra
session_1.text: Ha, true. If they do reply over the break, I'll deal with it when I'm back.

session_1.speaker: Yusuf
session_1.text: Sounds good. Enjoy the long weekend then.

session_1.speaker: Petra
session_1.text: You too, Yusuf. Talk soon!

session_2.speaker: Petra
session_2.text: Morning Yusuf! How was your weekend? Did you manage to get any rest?

session_2.speaker: Yusuf
session_2.text: Morning! Mostly yes, though I spent Sunday going through some old files and found the paperwork from that distribution deal we did years ago. Remember the one with the very stubborn counterparty?

session_2.speaker: Petra
session_2.text: Ha, how could I forget. We went through something like nine drafts of one paragraph. I still think we won that argument on points.

session_2.speaker: Yusuf
session_2.text: We did, barely. Anyway, good reminder of why I like having you on this one too.

session_2.speaker: Petra
session_2.text: Flattery noted. Speaking of this one, the liability cap has changed and is now $750,000.

session_2.speaker: Yusuf
session_2.text: Okay, good to know. I'll flag it to our finance people this week so they're not caught off guard.

session_2.speaker: Petra
session_2.text: Sounds good. By the way, are you still planning to have me visit the plant? You mentioned it last time.

session_2.speaker: Yusuf
session_2.text: Yes, definitely. Come out in a couple of weeks if you can. I'd love for you to see the production floor, it helps to understand what we're actually protecting in all this paperwork.

session_2.speaker: Petra
session_2.text: I'd like that. I'll check my calendar and send a few slots. Should I bring boots or is it more of a hard hat and lanyard situation?

session_2.speaker: Yusuf
session_2.text: Hard hat and safety glasses, we'll supply both. Just wear shoes you don't mind getting a bit dusty.

session_2.speaker: Petra
session_2.text: Perfect. Oh, and a heads up that my office closes for a few days over the holiday coming up, so I'll be slow to reply then.

session_2.speaker: Yusuf
session_2.text: Noted. We shut the plant that same stretch, so honestly I'll be offline too. Before that, one thing I wanted to mention: the agreement includes an exclusivity clause, and I want to make sure we talk it through properly.

session_2.speaker: Petra
session_2.text: Fair enough, let's put time aside for it soon. I'll come to the plant visit with questions ready.

session_2.speaker: Yusuf
session_2.text: Great, that works for me. I'll have our operations lead join so you can ask him anything directly.

session_2.speaker: Petra
session_2.text: Wonderful. I'll send those calendar slots later today.

session_2.speaker: Yusuf
session_2.text: Thanks Petra. Talk soon!

session_3.speaker: Petra
session_3.text: Hi Yusuf, quick one before we get into it: our office is shut next Friday for the holiday, so if you need me then, shoot me a message before Thursday evening.

session_3.speaker: Yusuf
session_3.text: Noted, thanks. Honestly I'm planning to be offline most of that day anyway.

session_3.speaker: Petra
session_3.text: Good plan. On the draft, the delivery clause now names Antwerp as where the goods get dropped off.

session_3.speaker: Yusuf
session_3.text: Okay, that works for our logistics people. Did Marlow say anything about the draft yet?

session_3.speaker: Petra
session_3.text: Not a word. It's been almost ten days since I sent my last email and I've had nothing back, not even an acknowledgement.

session_3.speaker: Yusuf
session_3.text: Ugh, typical. They took forever last time too, I remember waiting over a week just for a one-line answer.

session_3.speaker: Petra
session_3.text: I'll chase them again tomorrow morning. If they keep stalling we may need to put a soft deadline on their response.

session_3.speaker: Yusuf
session_3.text: Fine by me. One thing I wanted to confirm so we're on the same page: the agreement runs under Ontario law.

session_3.speaker: Petra
session_3.text: Got it, I'll keep that in mind as I go through their comments when they finally arrive.

session_3.speaker: Yusuf
session_3.text: Also, the minimum we commit to each year is 55,000 units. That's settled on our side, no more debating it internally.

session_3.speaker: Petra
session_3.text: Understood, I'll treat that as fixed from here on.

session_3.speaker: Yusuf
session_3.text: And for payment, we're going with 45 days.

session_3.speaker: Petra
session_3.text: Great, that's clear. Should we book the next call for the week after the closure? I'm fairly open on Tuesday or Wednesday.

session_3.speaker: Yusuf
session_3.text: Wednesday afternoon is better for me, I've got a standing meeting Tuesday.

session_3.speaker: Petra
session_3.text: Wednesday afternoon it is. I'll send over an invite shortly.

session_3.speaker: Yusuf
session_3.text: Perfect, talk then. Enjoy the long weekend!

session_4.speaker: Yusuf
session_4.text: Hey Petra, quick one before the weekend. Is your office closed over the Easter break? I want to know when I can reach you.

session_4.speaker: Petra
session_4.text: We close from the Thursday before Easter through the Monday after. I'll still check email once a day, so nothing will sit for long.

session_4.speaker: Yusuf
session_4.text: Good to know. By the way, I've been meaning to ask: the person who signs for Marlow Ltd is Ms. Devereux, so you can put her name in the signature block.

session_4.speaker: Petra
session_4.text: Noted, I'll draft it that way. Are you free for a call next week to walk through the latest draft?

session_4.speaker: Yusuf
session_4.text: Yes, Wednesday afternoon works. Also, you should come and see the plant sometime. We just reorganised the whole floor and it looks completely different.

session_4.speaker: Petra
session_4.text: I'd love that, I haven't been out there in ages. Maybe after the Easter break, once things calm down.

session_4.speaker: Yusuf
session_4.text: Sounds good. Oh, and I need to fix something I told you earlier. I made a mistake, the person signing for Marlow Ltd is not Ms. Devereux. It's Mr. Nakagawa.

session_4.speaker: Petra
session_4.text: No problem, glad you caught it before it went anywhere. I'll update the signature block today.

session_4.speaker: Yusuf
session_4.text: Thanks. One more correction while I'm at it. I said Ontario law for the agreement, and that was wrong. It's Swiss law.

session_4.speaker: Petra
session_4.text: Okay, thanks for flagging it. I'll adjust the draft accordingly and send you a clean copy.

session_4.speaker: Yusuf
session_4.text: Appreciate it. Do you remember that old deal we did years back with the packaging supplier? I was digging through some files and found the paperwork.

session_4.speaker: Petra
session_4.text: Of course I remember, that one dragged on for months. We both aged a few years during those negotiations.

session_4.speaker: Yusuf
session_4.text: Ha, true. Oh, I almost forgot to mention, there's an escrow arrangement for the tooling costs. Can you make sure the draft reflects that?

session_4.speaker: Petra
session_4.text: Will do. I'll add it in when I revise the draft and flag it in my cover note so it doesn't get lost.

session_4.speaker: Yusuf
session_4.text: Perfect. Talk Wednesday then, and enjoy the weekend.

session_4.speaker: Petra
session_4.text: You too, Yusuf. Talk soon.

session_5.speaker: Yusuf
session_5.text: Hi Petra, hope your weekend's going okay. Quick one before the week starts.

session_5.speaker: Petra
session_5.text: Hi Yusuf, it's been a quiet one, thanks. What's on your mind?

session_5.speaker: Yusuf
session_5.text: Marlow came back on Friday with a new one for us to deal with: the insurance certificates. I didn't expect that to come up this late.

session_5.speaker: Petra
session_5.text: Okay, thanks for flagging it. Can you forward me exactly what they sent? I'll have a look first thing tomorrow.

session_5.speaker: Yusuf
session_5.text: Will do, I'll send it over tonight. Honestly they're so slow to reply, we waited nearly a week for that one.

session_5.speaker: Petra
session_5.text: Yes, that's been the pattern. I wouldn't read too much into it, but it does eat into our timeline.

session_5.speaker: Yusuf
session_5.text: True. Anyway, we had a visit at the plant on Thursday, a few people from the operations side came to see the production line.

session_5.speaker: Petra
session_5.text: Oh nice, how did it go? Was it useful to have them see the setup in person?

session_5.speaker: Yusuf
session_5.text: It went well. The agreement covers the supply of ceramic bearings, so it really helped that they could see where those get tested and packed.

session_5.speaker: Petra
session_5.text: That's good to hear. Seeing the process usually makes people a bit more relaxed in the negotiation too.

session_5.speaker: Yusuf
session_5.text: Agreed, the mood was definitely better afterwards. Should we book the next call? I'm fairly free in the middle of next week.

session_5.speaker: Petra
session_5.text: Wednesday afternoon works for me. Does around three suit you?

session_5.speaker: Yusuf
session_5.text: Three on Wednesday is fine. I'll put it in my calendar now.

session_5.speaker: Petra
session_5.text: Great, I'll send the invite. And I'll chase Marlow's side again so we're not waiting on them.

session_5.speaker: Yusuf
session_5.text: Thanks Petra, appreciate it. Talk Wednesday then.

session_5.speaker: Petra
session_5.text: Speak then, enjoy the rest of your Sunday!

session_6.speaker: Petra
session_6.text: Morning Yusuf! Did you get any sleep after that flight back, or are you running on coffee again?

session_6.speaker: Yusuf
session_6.text: Coffee, mostly. The jet lag hit me harder than I expected this time.

session_6.speaker: Petra
session_6.text: Understandable. By the way, I was digging through some old files and came across the deal we did together back in the day with the distributor. Remember how that dragged on for months over a single comma?

session_6.speaker: Yusuf
session_6.text: Ha, I do remember. You were the only one who stayed calm in that room. I still think the comma won in the end.

session_6.speaker: Petra
session_6.text: It usually does. Anyway, one thing to flag from today's call: the port the goods are delivered to is now Bilbao.

session_6.speaker: Yusuf
session_6.text: Okay, noted. That should actually suit our logistics people better, I think.

session_6.speaker: Petra
session_6.text: Good to hear. And as I understand it, the minimum annual order volume is 70,000 units, and it's been that all along.

session_6.speaker: Yusuf
session_6.text: Right. Speaking of logistics, my team is closed next week for the holiday, so I'll be hard to reach until Tuesday.

session_6.speaker: Petra
session_6.text: No problem, enjoy the break. Our office is shut Monday as well, so nothing will move much on my side either.

session_6.speaker: Yusuf
session_6.text: Perfect, a proper pause for once. Are you doing anything nice with the day off?

session_6.speaker: Petra
session_6.text: Probably just a long walk and far too much reading. What about you?

session_6.speaker: Yusuf
session_6.text: Family lunch, I think. Oh, and before I forget, a new open point came up on our side in the negotiation: the tooling ownership.

session_6.speaker: Petra
session_6.text: Thanks for telling me. I'll think about how we want to approach it before we talk again.

session_6.speaker: Yusuf
session_6.text: Sounds good. Also, I'd love for you to come see the plant sometime. We finally finished the new floor layout.

session_6.speaker: Petra
session_6.text: I'd really like that. Let's find a slot once things calm down after the break.

session_6.speaker: Yusuf
session_6.text: Deal. I'll even arrange a proper tour and lunch in the canteen, which is better than it sounds.

session_6.speaker: Petra
session_6.text: Now I'm definitely coming. Talk in a couple of weeks, Yusuf, take care!

session_7.speaker: Yusuf
session_7.text: Morning Petra. Still nothing back from Marlow, it's been over a week now. Is it just me or are they getting slower every time?

session_7.speaker: Petra
session_7.text: Not just you. I sent a one-line question last Tuesday and I'm still waiting on an answer. Silence seems to be their default setting.

session_7.speaker: Yusuf
session_7.text: Reminds me of that old deal we did years back, the one with the warehouse people. They'd take a fortnight to confirm a lunch order.

session_7.speaker: Petra
session_7.text: Ha, I remember that one. You had me chasing them for what felt like months over a single signature page.

session_7.speaker: Yusuf
session_7.text: And somehow it still closed. Anyway, I spoke to our finance director yesterday, and the liability cap has moved, it's $1.2 million now.

session_7.speaker: Petra
session_7.text: Good to know, thanks for telling me straight away. I'll make sure the draft reflects that before anything goes back across.

session_7.speaker: Yusuf
session_7.text: Perfect. Did you get a chance to read through the latest version end to end?

session_7.speaker: Petra
session_7.text: I did, and I found a typo on the second page. A word was missing a letter and it changed the meaning of the sentence, which was a bit awkward.

session_7.speaker: Yusuf
session_7.text: Ha, that's the sort of thing that would have come back to bite us in a dispute. Good catch.

session_7.speaker: Petra
session_7.text: That's what you pay me for. I've fixed it in my copy, so the next version should be clean.

session_7.speaker: Yusuf
session_7.text: Great. Should I nudge their side, or would it look better coming from you?

session_7.speaker: Petra
session_7.text: I'd let me do it. A short, polite email from the lawyer tends to get a faster reply than a call from the client.

session_7.speaker: Yusuf
session_7.text: Fair enough. I'll leave it with you then. I'm travelling for the rest of the week anyway.

session_7.speaker: Petra
session_7.text: Safe travels. I'll send the nudge this afternoon and message you as soon as anything lands.

session_7.speaker: Yusuf
session_7.text: Thanks Petra. Speak in a couple of weeks, or sooner if they finally wake up.

session_7.speaker: Petra
session_7.text: Will do. Enjoy the trip!

session_8.speaker: Yusuf
session_8.text: Morning Petra. Quick random thing, I was clearing out a cabinet yesterday and found the folder from the Delmar deal. Remember that one?

session_8.speaker: Petra
session_8.text: Ha, how could I forget. Those were the months I lived on takeaway and redlines. Good outcome in the end though.

session_8.speaker: Yusuf
session_8.text: It really was. Anyway, I wanted to ask if you'd like to come out to the plant sometime. I think seeing the production floor would help you get a feel for how we actually work.

session_8.speaker: Petra
session_8.text: I'd love that. I've only ever seen the place in photos. Is there a good time, or does it depend on what's running?

session_8.speaker: Yusuf
session_8.text: Mid-week is best, the floor is calmer on Wednesdays and Thursdays. And our finance lead keeps asking when we can sit down with you, since the payment term is now 14 days and she wants to plan cash flow around it. But the visit itself would be mostly a walk-through and lunch.

session_8.speaker: Petra
session_8.text: Lunch is the part I'm sold on already. I'll check my diary and send you a couple of options for the visit.

session_8.speaker: Yusuf
session_8.text: Perfect. Fair warning, the canteen coffee is terrible, so we might sneak off somewhere nicer.

session_8.speaker: Petra
session_8.text: Noted, I'll bring my own thermos just in case. Should I wear anything particular? Steel toe boots, hi-vis, that kind of thing?

session_8.speaker: Yusuf
session_8.text: We'll kit you out at the door, hard hat and glasses and all. You'll look very official.

session_8.speaker: Petra
session_8.text: Great, I've always wanted an excuse to wear a hard hat to work. Shall we pencil in our next call before I forget?

session_8.speaker: Yusuf
session_8.text: Yes please. I'm travelling the early part of next week, so anything from Wednesday onward suits me better.

session_8.speaker: Petra
session_8.text: Wednesday afternoon works for me. Say around two?

session_8.speaker: Yusuf
session_8.text: Two is good. I'll put it in my calendar now so it doesn't get swallowed by something else.

session_8.speaker: Petra
session_8.text: Brilliant. I'll send an invite as well so we both have it. And I'll get you those plant visit dates by Friday.

session_8.speaker: Yusuf
session_8.text: Sounds like a plan. Thanks Petra, talk Wednesday.

session_8.speaker: Petra
session_8.text: Talk then, enjoy the rest of your week!

session_9.speaker: Yusuf
session_9.text: Morning Petra. Quick one before I forget: I spotted a typo in the latest draft, page 14 has "the the" in the middle of a sentence.

session_9.speaker: Petra
session_9.text: Ha, good catch. I'll fix that in the next turn of the document along with a couple of formatting glitches I noticed.

session_9.speaker: Yusuf
session_9.text: Perfect. Oh, and heads up, they've now come back and raised something new on the force majeure list. They want to add a few more events to it.

session_9.speaker: Petra
session_9.text: Okay, noted. I'd expected something like that to surface eventually. Can you forward me whatever they sent so I can see exactly what they're asking for?

session_9.speaker: Yusuf
session_9.text: Sure, it was just a short email, I'll send it over after this chat. Honestly it took them almost a week to even send that.

session_9.speaker: Petra
session_9.text: Yes, they're painfully slow. I sent a simple question on Monday and I'm still waiting for an answer.

session_9.speaker: Yusuf
session_9.text: Same experience here. Do you think they're doing it on purpose to wear us down?

session_9.speaker: Petra
session_9.text: Maybe a bit, or it's just internal sign-offs on their side. Either way I wouldn't read too much into it.

session_9.speaker: Yusuf
session_9.text: Fair enough. Now, when we eventually get to signing, how do you want to handle it? Do I need to print everything myself?

session_9.speaker: Petra
session_9.text: I'd suggest I send you a clean PDF and you print it, sign the signature page in blue ink, and scan it back to me. Original copies can follow by post if they insist.

session_9.speaker: Yusuf
session_9.text: Blue ink, got it. My printer is temperamental though, so I might just run it to the print shop down the road.

session_9.speaker: Petra
session_9.text: That works too. Just make sure it's single-sided and nothing gets scaled down, otherwise the page numbers look odd.

session_9.speaker: Yusuf
session_9.text: Will do. Should I initial every page or only the last one?

session_9.speaker: Petra
session_9.text: Only the signature page needs your full signature, but initialling each page is a nice extra if you have the patience.

session_9.speaker: Yusuf
session_9.text: I have plenty of patience compared to Marlow, apparently. I'll get you that email this afternoon.

session_9.speaker: Petra
session_9.text: Great, thanks Yusuf. Talk in a couple of weeks, or sooner if they surprise us with a quick reply.

session_10.speaker: Yusuf
session_10.text: Hi Petra, hope your week's going alright. Are you around on Monday, or is the office shut for the bank holiday?

session_10.speaker: Petra
session_10.text: We're closed Monday, yes, back Tuesday morning. I'll still be checking my phone though, so ping me if anything urgent comes up.

session_10.speaker: Yusuf
session_10.text: Good to know. I'm taking Monday off too, finally going to fix the shed roof before the rain comes back.

session_10.speaker: Petra
session_10.text: Ha, brave. Last time I tried a roof repair I ended up calling someone anyway.

session_10.speaker: Yusuf
session_10.text: Right, one thing I should tell you before I forget. The port the goods are delivered to has changed, it's Gdansk now.

session_10.speaker: Petra
session_10.text: Noted, thanks for flagging it. I'll make sure the paperwork reflects that.

session_10.speaker: Yusuf
session_10.text: Great. Oh, and we also got the point about the force majeure list settled, so that's one less thing hanging around.

session_10.speaker: Petra
session_10.text: Good, that's a relief. I'll update my notes on my side.

session_10.speaker: Yusuf
session_10.text: Now for the boring bit: how do you want to handle signing? Do I need to print everything out myself?

session_10.speaker: Petra
session_10.text: When we get there, I'd send you a clean PDF and you print it, sign in blue ink, and scan it back. Wet ink on every page where there's an initial box.

session_10.speaker: Yusuf
session_10.text: Blue ink, got it. My printer hates me though, it jams every time I need it for something important.

session_10.speaker: Petra
session_10.text: There's a print shop near your office, isn't there? Might be safer than trusting the printer.

session_10.speaker: Yusuf
session_10.text: Good call. By the way, this reminds me of that old distribution deal we did years ago, the one with the warehouse in the north. Remember the fax machine saga?

session_10.speaker: Petra
session_10.text: Oh god, I'd blocked that out. Three hours waiting for a fax to go through, and then it arrived upside down.

session_10.speaker: Yusuf
session_10.text: And we both just stood there laughing at it. Honestly that was one of the smoother deals despite all that.

session_10.speaker: Petra
session_10.text: It really was. Anyway, enjoy the long weekend, and good luck with the roof. Talk in a couple of weeks.

session_11.speaker: Yusuf
session_11.text: Morning Petra. Still nothing back from Marlow on the last thing I sent, it's been days. Is it just me or are they getting slower every time?

session_11.speaker: Petra
session_11.text: Not just you. They took nearly a week to answer my last email too, and it was a one-liner. I've stopped expecting quick turnarounds from them.

session_11.speaker: Yusuf
session_11.text: Honestly it reminds me of a deal I did years ago with a textile supplier. Every reply took ages and then arrived at 6pm on a Friday.

session_11.speaker: Petra
session_11.text: Ha, the classic Friday evening drop. Did that one ever close?

session_11.speaker: Yusuf
session_11.text: Eventually, yes, but I aged about five years in the process. Anyway, one thing I did hear from their side: the port the goods are delivered to is now Rotterdam, they switched it.

session_11.speaker: Petra
session_11.text: Okay, good to know, thanks for flagging it. I'll make sure the paperwork reflects that.

session_11.speaker: Yusuf
session_11.text: Great. How's your week looking, by the way? You sounded swamped on the phone last time.

session_11.speaker: Petra
session_11.text: Swamped is the word. I've got three matters landing at once and a hearing prep on top, so I'm basically living on coffee right now.

session_11.speaker: Yusuf
session_11.text: That sounds rough. I appreciate you still keeping on top of ours. Oh, and they also confirmed the exclusivity clause was removed from the agreement.

session_11.speaker: Petra
session_11.text: Noted, I'll update my draft accordingly. Did they say anything about why?

session_11.speaker: Yusuf
session_11.text: Not really, just a brief note saying it was gone. You know how they communicate, short and unexplained.

session_11.speaker: Petra
session_11.text: Right, which fits the pattern. I'd rather have the reasoning in writing but I'll work with it.

session_11.speaker: Yusuf
session_11.text: One more thing, they've just raised a new open point in the negotiation: the delivery penalties.

session_11.speaker: Petra
session_11.text: Okay, I'll look at what they're proposing and come back to you with my thoughts. Probably early next week given my schedule.

session_11.speaker: Yusuf
session_11.text: No rush, I know you're buried. Thanks Petra, talk in a couple of weeks or sooner if something moves.

session_11.speaker: Petra
session_11.text: Sounds good. Try to enjoy the rest of your week, and I'll ping you if Marlow finally wakes up.

session_12.speaker: Yusuf
session_12.text: Hi Petra, hope your week is going alright. Mine has been all over the place.

session_12.speaker: Petra
session_12.text: Hi Yusuf, can't complain, though it's been busy. What's been eating up your week?

session_12.speaker: Yusuf
session_12.text: Mostly prepping the plant for a visit. Our new operations manager is coming through on Thursday and everyone is scrubbing floors like it's a royal inspection.

session_12.speaker: Petra
session_12.text: Ha, I remember my visit there. You made me wear the biggest hard hat they had and I looked ridiculous.

session_12.speaker: Yusuf
session_12.text: That hat is legendary now. Someone stuck a photo of you in it on the canteen noticeboard and nobody has had the heart to take it down.

session_12.speaker: Petra
session_12.text: Oh no. Please tell me it's at least a flattering angle.

session_12.speaker: Yusuf
session_12.text: Not even slightly. Anyway, business: the Marlow side came back to us yesterday and they've raised something new, the audit rights. Wasn't on anyone's radar before.

session_12.speaker: Petra
session_12.text: Interesting, thanks for flagging it. Did they say what's behind it, or was it just dropped in an email?

session_12.speaker: Yusuf
session_12.text: Just a short note really, no explanation. I figured you'd want to see it before I said anything back.

session_12.speaker: Petra
session_12.text: Good instinct. Forward it over and I'll read it properly tonight, then we can decide how to respond.

session_12.speaker: Yusuf
session_12.text: Will do, sending it right after this chat. Did you ever get through that latest draft I sent?

session_12.speaker: Petra
session_12.text: I did, and I found a typo on page two. A date in the header says 2052 instead of 2025, so unless we're signing from the future, it needs fixing.

session_12.speaker: Yusuf
session_12.text: Ha, good catch. I read that page three times and never saw it.

session_12.speaker: Petra
session_12.text: That's what a second pair of eyes is for. It reminds me of the old distribution deal we did years ago, where a single misplaced comma nearly cost us a whole clause.

session_12.speaker: Yusuf
session_12.text: Don't remind me, I still have nightmares about that one. We were up until midnight arguing over punctuation.

session_12.speaker: Petra
session_12.text: And we won, so it was worth it. Okay, I'll get the typo fixed and send you a clean version tomorrow.

session_12.speaker: Yusuf
session_12.text: Perfect, thanks Petra. Talk in a couple of weeks, and good luck with the hard hat photo.

session_13.speaker: Yusuf
session_13.text: Morning Petra. Still no word back from the other side on anything, it's been over a week now.

session_13.speaker: Petra
session_13.text: Same here, they're painfully slow. I sent a nudge on Monday and got an out-of-office in return.

session_13.speaker: Yusuf
session_13.text: Classic. Honestly it reminds me of that old deal I did years back, the one with the packaging firm. Took them three months just to agree on a font for the contract.

session_13.speaker: Petra
session_13.text: Ha, I remember you telling me about that one. Did it ever close in the end?

session_13.speaker: Yusuf
session_13.text: It did, but we both aged a few years doing it. Anyway, one thing I should tell you: the liability cap has moved, it's $5 million now.

session_13.speaker: Petra
session_13.text: Okay, good to know. I'll make sure the working draft reflects that before anything else goes out.

session_13.speaker: Yusuf
session_13.text: Thanks. Also, I finally found out who's acting for Marlow. It's Hartwell Breck.

session_13.speaker: Petra
session_13.text: Right, that helps. I'll reach out to them directly rather than going through Marlow's people.

session_13.speaker: Yusuf
session_13.text: Sounds good. Are you still free to come out to the plant sometime this month? I'd love to show you the production floor.

session_13.speaker: Petra
session_13.text: I'd really like that. It's always easier to draft sensibly when I've seen how things actually run.

session_13.speaker: Yusuf
session_13.text: Great. The tour takes about an hour and I'll put on proper coffee, not the machine stuff.

session_13.speaker: Petra
session_13.text: Now you're talking. Should I bring a hard hat or do you supply those?

session_13.speaker: Yusuf
session_13.text: We've got plenty, though they're all a bit scuffed. Safety boots too if you don't have any.

session_13.speaker: Petra
session_13.text: Perfect. I'll check my diary tonight and suggest a couple of days.

session_13.speaker: Yusuf
session_13.text: Brilliant, just let me know. Speak in a couple of weeks otherwise?

session_13.speaker: Petra
session_13.text: Yes, I'll ping you if anything lands from their side before then. Take care, Yusuf.

session_14.speaker: Yusuf
session_14.text: Morning Petra. Still nothing back from Marlow, which is getting a bit ridiculous. Is it just me or are they slower every time?

session_14.speaker: Petra
session_14.text: Not just you. I sent my last note almost two weeks ago and got a one-line acknowledgement back, nothing more.

session_14.speaker: Yusuf
session_14.text: Two weeks for a one-liner. I'd be embarrassed.

session_14.speaker: Petra
session_14.text: Ha, I doubt they are. How's your week going, by the way?

session_14.speaker: Yusuf
session_14.text: Busy but fine. Mostly chasing suppliers, so I can't really complain about anyone else chasing. How about you, are you drowning?

session_14.speaker: Petra
session_14.text: Fairly close. I've got three other matters all wanting attention at once, so your draft has been getting read in the gaps between calls.

session_14.speaker: Yusuf
session_14.text: I appreciate you squeezing it in. I did read through the latest version last night, by the way.

session_14.speaker: Petra
session_14.text: Good, did anything jump out at you?

session_14.speaker: Yusuf
session_14.text: Only a typo, really. In the definitions section there's a word that's missing a letter, and it made me read the sentence twice.

session_14.speaker: Petra
session_14.text: Ah, thanks for catching that. I've read that page so many times my eyes just slide over it.

session_14.speaker: Yusuf
session_14.text: That's the problem with your own drafts. Fresh eyes spot it right away.

session_14.speaker: Petra
session_14.text: True. I'll fix it and run a proper proofread before it goes back out, so it doesn't look sloppy when it lands with them.

session_14.speaker: Yusuf
session_14.text: Sounds good. Do you think we'll hear from them this week, or should I plan on another long wait?

session_14.speaker: Petra
session_14.text: I'd plan on the wait, honestly, but I'll nudge them again on Friday if it's still quiet.

session_14.speaker: Yusuf
session_14.text: Perfect, a polite nudge is all we can do. Thanks Petra, talk in a couple of weeks.

session_14.speaker: Petra
session_14.text: Will do. Enjoy the rest of your week, and I'll send the corrected draft once it's cleaned up.

session_15.speaker: Yusuf
session_15.text: Morning Petra! Quick thing first: I was reading through the latest draft last night and spotted a typo on page four, 'agrement' with a missing e.

session_15.speaker: Petra
session_15.text: Good catch, thanks. I'll fix it in the next version. Honestly I've read that page so many times my eyes just glide over it.

session_15.speaker: Yusuf
session_15.text: Ha, same here, I only noticed because the spellcheck underlined it in red.

session_15.speaker: Petra
session_15.text: Fair enough. Anything else jump out at you while you were reading?

session_15.speaker: Yusuf
session_15.text: Nothing else that looked wrong. Oh, and I talked to our ops team yesterday and the delivery penalties are settled as far as we're concerned, so I'm happy to move on from that.

session_15.speaker: Petra
session_15.text: Great, that's a relief to hear. I'll make a note of it on my side.

session_15.speaker: Yusuf
session_15.text: Now the practical stuff. How do you want to handle printing and signing? Do I need to print the whole thing or just the signature pages?

session_15.speaker: Petra
session_15.text: Just the signature pages is fine, but print them single-sided, please. I'll send a PDF with the pages flagged so you don't have to hunt for them.

session_15.speaker: Yusuf
session_15.text: Perfect. Does it need blue ink, or is black okay? Our office printer has been temperamental lately.

session_15.speaker: Petra
session_15.text: Either works, though blue ink does make it obvious it's an original. Just don't use pencil, you'd be surprised how often I get asked.

session_15.speaker: Yusuf
session_15.text: Ha, no pencil, got it. I'll sign in front of someone at the office anyway so there's a witness if needed.

session_15.speaker: Petra
session_15.text: Sensible. By the way, you mentioned a while back that you wanted me to visit your plant at some point. Is that still on the table?

session_15.speaker: Yusuf
session_15.text: Absolutely, I'd love that. We could do a tour and then lunch in the canteen, the food there is better than you'd expect.

session_15.speaker: Petra
session_15.text: Now you're talking. I'd like to see the production floor properly, it helps me understand what I'm writing about.

session_15.speaker: Yusuf
session_15.text: Then let's aim for sometime in the next few weeks. I'll check the calendar and send you a couple of options.

session_15.speaker: Petra
session_15.text: Sounds good. I'll bring sturdy shoes and send the signature pages over this afternoon.

session_16.speaker: Yusuf
session_16.text: Hey Petra, I was reading through the latest draft last night and spotted a typo on the signature page. They've spelled my surname wrong.

session_16.speaker: Petra
session_16.text: Ha, good catch. I'll fix that right away, it's easy to miss when you've read the thing a dozen times.

session_16.speaker: Yusuf
session_16.text: No worries at all. I'd rather it's right before anything gets printed.

session_16.speaker: Petra
session_16.text: Agreed. I'll send you a clean version once it's corrected, and you can give it one last look.

session_16.speaker: Yusuf
session_16.text: Perfect. How are we handling the printing, by the way? Do you want me to print at my end or should your office do it?

session_16.speaker: Petra
session_16.text: I'd suggest we print it here and courier you the set. Our printer handles the double-sided pages properly, and I can tab where you need to sign.

session_16.speaker: Yusuf
session_16.text: Sounds good to me. Do I need a witness or can I just sign and send it back?

session_16.speaker: Petra
session_16.text: Just sign in blue ink if you can, so it's obvious which copy is the original. No witness needed on your side.

session_16.speaker: Yusuf
session_16.text: Blue ink, got it. I'll dig out a decent pen so it doesn't look like a scrawl.

session_16.speaker: Petra
session_16.text: Ha, a scrawl is perfectly legal, don't worry. Just keep the pages in order.

session_16.speaker: Yusuf
session_16.text: Will do. You sound a bit rushed today, are things hectic on your end?

session_16.speaker: Petra
session_16.text: A little. August is meant to be quiet but half my clients decided to close things before the holidays, so I've been buried all week.

session_16.speaker: Yusuf
session_16.text: Sorry to add to the pile. I really appreciate you fitting me in.

session_16.speaker: Petra
session_16.text: Not at all, you've been one of the easier ones, honestly. I'll get the corrected draft to you by tomorrow afternoon.

session_16.speaker: Yusuf
session_16.text: Great, thanks. And hopefully you get a proper break once this is out the door.

session_16.speaker: Petra
session_16.text: That's the plan. A long weekend somewhere with no laptop would be lovely.

session_1.speaker: Noor
session_1.text: Hi Edmund, it's Noor from the practice. Just checking in like we said. How's your week been?

session_1.speaker: Edmund
session_1.text: Hi Noor! Not bad at all, thanks. Bit chilly out but I can't complain.

session_1.speaker: Noor
session_1.text: Glad to hear it. Did you manage to get to the clinic okay last time? I know parking there can be a nightmare.

session_1.speaker: Edmund
session_1.text: Ha, it was. I drove around the block twice before a space opened up. I nearly gave up and walked from the next street over.

session_1.speaker: Noor
session_1.text: That's the usual story, sadly. Walking from the next street isn't a bad idea though, honestly.

session_1.speaker: Edmund
session_1.text: That's what I told myself. I've actually been trying to walk more lately, nothing dramatic, just getting out a bit most days.

session_1.speaker: Noor
session_1.text: That's great, and it all adds up. Do you find it easy to stick with, or does the weather put you off?

session_1.speaker: Edmund
session_1.text: Weather's the main excuse, I'll admit. But once I'm out there I'm always glad I went.

session_1.speaker: Noor
session_1.text: That's the way. And how about the eating side of things? Any changes you've noticed in your habits lately?

session_1.speaker: Edmund
session_1.text: Trying to be a bit more sensible, I suppose. Fewer biscuits with the tea, though I won't pretend I've given them up entirely.

session_1.speaker: Noor
session_1.text: Ha, nobody expects perfection. Small swaps like that tend to stick better than big overhauls.

session_1.speaker: Edmund
session_1.text: That's reassuring. My wife keeps an eye on me anyway, so it's hard to sneak much past her.

session_1.speaker: Noor
session_1.text: Good to have a bit of support at home. Meals regular enough for you, or do you find you skip things sometimes?

session_1.speaker: Edmund
session_1.text: Mostly regular. I try not to leave it too long between meals, otherwise I end up grazing on whatever's nearby.

session_1.speaker: Noor
session_1.text: Sounds like you're on a sensible track. I'll check in again in a couple of weeks, but message me before then if anything comes up.

session_1.speaker: Edmund
session_1.text: Will do. Thanks for the call, Noor, and good luck with the parking if I see you at the clinic!

session_2.speaker: Edmund
session_2.text: Morning Noor. Good to hear from you again.

session_2.speaker: Noor
session_2.text: Morning Edmund! How's the week treating you so far?

session_2.speaker: Edmund
session_2.text: Not bad at all. My granddaughter stayed over the weekend and she wore me out, she's got more energy than the whole street put together.

session_2.speaker: Noor
session_2.text: Ha, that sounds lovely though. What did you get up to?

session_2.speaker: Edmund
session_2.text: Mostly baking, if you can call it that. More flour on the floor than in the bowl. I did have to remind myself to keep to my one sensible slice.

session_2.speaker: Noor
session_2.text: Good for you. How have the meals been otherwise, any better routine day to day?

session_2.speaker: Edmund
session_2.text: Pretty steady, I'd say. More vegetables, fewer biscuits with the tea, and I've stopped eating late in the evening.

session_2.speaker: Noor
session_2.text: That's great to hear. Just to tick off my checklist, can you remind me what you're taking for the metformin each day?

session_2.speaker: Edmund
session_2.text: Yes, it's 750 mg a day, same as ever, I haven't missed any.

session_2.speaker: Noor
session_2.text: Perfect. And where do you pick up your prescriptions these days? I want my notes to be right.

session_2.speaker: Edmund
session_2.text: That'd be Calder Pharmacy, down past the library.

session_2.speaker: Noor
session_2.text: Lovely, I'll jot that down. How about the sleeping, are you getting a decent night?

session_2.speaker: Edmund
session_2.text: Oh hold on, I got that wrong earlier, sorry. It's not Calder Pharmacy, that was a slip on my part. I collect everything from Oakfield Pharmacy.

session_2.speaker: Noor
session_2.text: No worries at all, I've changed it in my notes. So, the sleep?

session_2.speaker: Edmund
session_2.text: Better than last time, actually. I'm dropping off around eleven and only waking once, then back to sleep fairly quickly.

session_2.speaker: Noor
session_2.text: That's a good improvement. Keep it up, and I'll check in with you again in a couple of weeks. Enjoy the rest of your day, and give that granddaughter a hug from me!

session_3.speaker: Noor
session_3.text: Hi Edmund, it's Noor from the practice. Just checking in for our usual catch-up. How's your week going?

session_3.speaker: Edmund
session_3.text: Hello Noor. Not bad at all, thanks. A bit tired but I think half the street is the same.

session_3.speaker: Noor
session_3.text: Ha, yes, it's been going round. We've had a lot of people in with flu this season, so the waiting room has been full of tissues and sniffles.

session_3.speaker: Edmund
session_3.text: I've been dodging it so far. Washing my hands like a surgeon and staying away from my neighbour's grandkids.

session_3.speaker: Noor
session_3.text: Smart plan. Did you get the text reminder about your next appointment, by the way? We switched over to the new system recently.

session_3.speaker: Edmund
session_3.text: I did, yes. It came through on my phone on Monday. Much better than the old one, which used to ring me at suppertime.

session_3.speaker: Noor
session_3.text: Good to hear. It's supposed to send a second nudge the day before too, so let me know if that doesn't turn up.

session_3.speaker: Edmund
session_3.text: Will do. Oh, is the lift at the clinic still out? I was there last week and there was a sign taped to it.

session_3.speaker: Noor
session_3.text: Still broken, I'm afraid. They say the engineer is coming soon, but we've heard that before. If stairs are a problem, we can bring you down to a ground floor room.

session_3.speaker: Edmund
session_3.text: Stairs are fine for me, it's just my knees complaining a bit on the way up. I'll take it slow.

session_3.speaker: Noor
session_3.text: No rush at all. Honestly, if you'd rather we set you up in one of the downstairs rooms, just say so when you arrive and the front desk will sort it.

session_3.speaker: Edmund
session_3.text: That's kind of you. I'll keep it in mind if the knees get worse.

session_3.speaker: Noor
session_3.text: Perfect. Is there anything else you wanted to chat about today, or shall I let you get on with your afternoon?

session_3.speaker: Edmund
session_3.text: Nothing else from me. Just glad the reminders are working now.

session_3.speaker: Noor
session_3.text: Great. Take care, keep dodging that flu, and I'll message again in a couple of weeks.

session_3.speaker: Edmund
session_3.text: Thanks Noor, talk soon.

session_4.speaker: Noor
session_4.text: Morning Edmund, it's Noor from the practice. How's the week been treating you?

session_4.speaker: Edmund
session_4.text: Morning Noor! Not bad at all, bit chilly but I can't complain.

session_4.speaker: Noor
session_4.text: Good to hear. How have you been getting on with the eating lately? Any struggles?

session_4.speaker: Edmund
session_4.text: Pretty steady really. I've been sticking to smaller plates and cutting back on the biscuits, though Sundays are still a bit of a free for all.

session_4.speaker: Noor
session_4.text: Ha, Sundays are allowed a little leeway. Small plates is a clever trick, honestly.

session_4.speaker: Edmund
session_4.text: My wife's idea. Oh, I got my latest blood test back by the way, the HbA1c came in at 7.9%.

session_4.speaker: Noor
session_4.text: Thanks for telling me, that's useful to have. We'll talk it through properly at the next review, but keep doing what you're doing in the meantime.

session_4.speaker: Edmund
session_4.text: Will do. I've also been walking a lot more, nearly every morning down by the river before breakfast.

session_4.speaker: Noor
session_4.text: That's brilliant, Edmund. Morning walks are one of the easiest habits to keep up once they stick.

session_4.speaker: Edmund
session_4.text: Yes, I actually look forward to it now. The dog certainly approves too.

session_4.speaker: Noor
session_4.text: Ha, a happy dog is a good motivator. Anything else new on your side?

session_4.speaker: Edmund
session_4.text: One thing, I started taking omega-3 a little while back. Figured it couldn't hurt.

session_4.speaker: Noor
session_4.text: Okay, noted. Just keep me posted on anything new you start taking, and we'll keep an eye on how you feel.

session_4.speaker: Edmund
session_4.text: Will do. Is the flu jab still on offer, or has the season passed?

session_4.speaker: Noor
session_4.text: The main flu season's winding down now, so the jabs have mostly finished for this year. It's worth remembering for the autumn, though.

session_4.speaker: Edmund
session_4.text: Right, I'll put a reminder in my diary for then. Thanks for the call, Noor.

session_4.speaker: Noor
session_4.text: Any time, Edmund. Speak in a couple of weeks, take care!

session_5.speaker: Noor
session_5.text: Morning Edmund, it's Noor from the practice. How have you been keeping this fortnight?

session_5.speaker: Edmund
session_5.text: Morning Noor. Can't complain, bit tired but I put that down to my granddaughter. She stayed over at the weekend and ran me ragged.

session_5.speaker: Noor
session_5.text: Ha, that'll do it. How old is she now, is she still into everything?

session_5.speaker: Edmund
