session_1.speaker: Ffion
session_1.text: Morning Leandro! Did you see the window display when you walked past last night? I finally swapped the old banner for the new frame we found in the back.

session_1.speaker: Leandro
session_1.text: I did, it looks loads better. The red frame really catches your eye from across the road.

session_1.speaker: Ffion
session_1.text: That was the idea. I might hang a few helmets off the handlebars too, make it look a bit more lived in.

session_1.speaker: Leandro
session_1.text: Good call. Maybe add a little sign about the race on Saturday week? Half the club is doing it.

session_1.speaker: Ffion
session_1.text: Ha, yes, the local ten-mile thing. Are you riding it or just standing at the finish with a flask?

session_1.speaker: Leandro
session_1.text: Flask, definitely. My legs haven't recovered from the last time I tried to keep up with those lot.

session_1.speaker: Ffion
session_1.text: Fair enough. Oh, before I forget, I've got a couple of online orders to pack up this afternoon. Those all go out with Parcelwing, so the labels are in the drawer under the counter.

session_1.speaker: Leandro
session_1.text: Got it, I'll sort them after lunch. Is the big box for the wheelset still sitting by the door?

session_1.speaker: Ffion
session_1.text: That's the one. Wrap it well, it's a long way to travel.

session_1.speaker: Leandro
session_1.text: Will do. By the way, we've had loads of people in with punctures since the roadworks started on the high street.

session_1.speaker: Ffion
session_1.text: I noticed! It must be all the grit and bits of metal they've left in the gutter. Three people came in on Monday alone.

session_1.speaker: Leandro
session_1.text: I've been telling everyone to check their tyres for embedded stuff before they ride off. Most of them just shrug.

session_1.speaker: Ffion
session_1.text: Maybe we should put a note by the till about it. Something friendly, not preachy.

session_1.speaker: Leandro
session_1.text: I can scribble one up with a little drawing of a sad tyre. Customers like that sort of thing.

session_1.speaker: Ffion
session_1.text: Perfect, do it. Right, kettle's on, want a tea before we open?

session_1.speaker: Leandro
session_1.text: Yes please, two sugars. I'll get the sign started while it brews.

session_2.speaker: Ffion
session_2.text: Morning Leandro. Did you see the van parked right across our door again? I had to squeeze in sideways with my coffee.

session_2.speaker: Leandro
session_2.text: Ha, yes. I got in early and it was already there, engine running and nobody in sight. I went and knocked on the cafe next door and it turned out to be theirs.

session_2.speaker: Ffion
session_2.text: Of course it was. Did they at least say sorry?

session_2.speaker: Leandro
session_2.text: The driver came out looking sheepish and moved it about ten minutes later. I think he'll think twice next week.

session_2.speaker: Ffion
session_2.text: Good. Anyway, I've been meaning to ask if you're still up for the charity ride next month? I told the organisers we'd put a little stand out.

session_2.speaker: Leandro
session_2.text: Definitely, I'm in. I'll bring the foldable gazebo from my garage so we're not standing in the rain like last time.

session_2.speaker: Ffion
session_2.text: Brilliant, last time my sandwich went soggy and I've not forgiven the weather since.

session_2.speaker: Leandro
session_2.text: Fair enough. Do you think we should do a quick free safety check for anyone riding? People always turn up with a flat or a loose saddle.

session_2.speaker: Ffion
session_2.text: Yes, love that idea. It's good for the riders and people see us doing something useful.

session_2.speaker: Leandro
session_2.text: Also, are you going to the local race on Saturday? A couple of the regulars are entering and I promised I'd cheer them on.

session_2.speaker: Ffion
session_2.text: I'm hoping to pop along for an hour or so. I'll bring a flask and a loud voice.

session_2.speaker: Leandro
session_2.text: Perfect, the loud voice is half the job. The course goes up that nasty hill by the church, so it should be a good one to watch.

session_2.speaker: Ffion
session_2.text: Oh that hill is brutal. I'll be shouting extra loud there then.

session_2.speaker: Leandro
session_2.text: Ha, they'll need it. Should I keep an eye out for that van again before we open tomorrow?

session_2.speaker: Ffion
session_2.text: Yes please, and if it's back you have my full permission to stand in front of it dramatically.

session_2.speaker: Leandro
session_2.text: Deal. I'll bring my most disapproving face.

session_3.speaker: Ffion
session_3.text: Morning! Did you see the sign-up sheet for the Saturday race? Half the club's already put their names down.

session_3.speaker: Leandro
session_3.text: I did, it's going to be a busy week. People will want their bikes checked over before it.

session_3.speaker: Ffion
session_3.text: Yeah, and a couple of folks asked me yesterday what we charge, so just so we're on the same page, a basic service is $60 and that's not changing.

session_3.speaker: Leandro
session_3.text: Got it, I'll tell anyone who asks. Do you want me to put a little card up by the counter too?

session_3.speaker: Ffion
session_3.text: Good idea, nothing fancy, just something handwritten. Also did you hear about the charity ride next month?

session_3.speaker: Leandro
session_3.text: The one for the children's hospital? My cousin is doing the long route, she's been training all winter.

session_3.speaker: Ffion
session_3.text: That's the one. I thought we could put out a collection jar and maybe offer to check tyre pressures for the riders on the morning.

session_3.speaker: Leandro
session_3.text: Happy to do that. I can come in early if you want, the start's not far from the shop anyway.

session_3.speaker: Ffion
session_3.text: Brilliant, thank you. Oh, and that delivery van was blocking the door again yesterday, I had to ask the driver to move twice.

session_3.speaker: Leandro
session_3.text: Ha, I saw him when I came in this morning, parked right across the entrance with the hazards on. A customer nearly turned back.

session_3.speaker: Ffion
session_3.text: I'm going to mention it to Mrs. Pemberton, since she's our landlord and the loading bay out back is hers. Maybe she can have a word with the neighbours about where vans should stop.

session_3.speaker: Leandro
session_3.text: That would help a lot. The bay is always empty while the vans sit out front.

session_3.speaker: Ffion
session_3.text: Exactly. Anyway, can you open up on Friday? I've got a dentist appointment first thing.

session_3.speaker: Leandro
session_3.text: Sure, no problem. I'll sweep the pavement too and keep the door propped so it's obvious we're open.

session_3.speaker: Ffion
session_3.text: You're a star. I'll bring pastries to make up for it.

session_3.speaker: Leandro
session_3.text: Now you're talking. See you tomorrow!

session_4.speaker: Ffion
session_4.text: Morning! Sorry, I'm running about ten minutes late. There's a delivery van parked right across the shop door and the driver has vanished.

session_4.speaker: Leandro
session_4.text: Ha, I saw it when I came in. I squeezed past by the bins. Want me to go and look for him?

session_4.speaker: Ffion
session_4.text: Give it five minutes, he'll turn up. Did the kettle get sorted? I swear it was making that clicking noise again yesterday.

session_4.speaker: Leandro
session_4.text: Still clicking, but it boils. I gave the limescale a go with vinegar, didn't help much. Might just be on its last legs.

session_4.speaker: Ffion
session_4.text: Ugh. Fine, we'll get a new one before it dies mid-brew. Oh, and the van guy did come back, he's moving it now. Also, a box came in earlier and it's the Ribble Hybrid, finally, so it's sitting out the back waiting to be built up.

session_4.speaker: Leandro
session_4.text: Oh nice, that was a long wait. I'll make a start on it after I've dealt with the repair queue.

session_4.speaker: Ffion
session_4.text: No rush, do the repairs first. How did it go yesterday afternoon after I left? I felt bad dumping that grumpy man on you.

session_4.speaker: Leandro
session_4.text: Ha, the one who wanted his wheel trued for nothing because he'd 'only had it a week'? He wasn't happy.

session_4.speaker: Ffion
session_4.text: That's him. Did he calm down at all?

session_4.speaker: Leandro
session_4.text: Eventually. I explained it was a bent rim from hitting a kerb, not a build fault, and he went quiet. Then he asked if we could still look at it today.

session_4.speaker: Ffion
session_4.text: Of course he did. Is he coming in this morning, then?

session_4.speaker: Leandro
session_4.text: Said he'd be here around eleven. I'll put the wheel on the stand ready so it's not a long wait.

session_4.speaker: Ffion
session_4.text: Good plan. If he starts up again, just call me over and I'll take him. I'm better at the smiling-through-gritted-teeth thing.

session_4.speaker: Leandro
session_4.text: Deal. I'll stick the kettle on now, though. Might as well enjoy it while it still works.

session_4.speaker: Ffion
session_4.text: Make mine strong. I'll be there in two minutes, just finding somewhere to park now the van's gone.

session_5.speaker: Ffion
session_5.text: Morning! Did you see the van parked right across our door when you came in? It's been there since before I opened up.

session_5.speaker: Leandro
session_5.text: Yeah, I had to squeeze past the wing mirror to get the key in. I went and knocked on the cab window but nobody was in it.

session_5.speaker: Ffion
session_5.text: Typical. If it's still there at ten I'll ring the number on the side of it.

session_5.speaker: Leandro
session_5.text: Fair enough. By the way, I was going through the paperwork folder yesterday and the monthly rent on the shop is $2,350, in case you wanted it for the spreadsheet.

session_5.speaker: Ffion
session_5.text: Oh good, thanks for checking that. I always forget to write it down anywhere I can actually find it.

session_5.speaker: Leandro
session_5.text: No worries. Also, I was thinking we should redo the window display this week. The sun has bleached the blue backdrop and it looks a bit sad now.

session_5.speaker: Ffion
session_5.text: Agreed, it's looking tired. Could you swap the fabric for the green one from the back cupboard? I'd like the red commuter bike front and centre.

session_5.speaker: Leandro
session_5.text: Sure, I'll do it after lunch when it's quiet. I'll wipe the glass inside and out too, it's covered in finger smudges.

session_5.speaker: Ffion
session_5.text: Perfect. And a customer asked me yesterday if we're open at the weekend, so I told her we're open on Sundays too, just so you know if anyone asks you.

session_5.speaker: Leandro
session_5.text: Good to know, I'll tell people the same. Do you want me to put a little sign in the window about it while I'm in there?

session_5.speaker: Ffion
session_5.text: Yes please, that's a nice idea. Something simple, black marker on white card is fine.

session_5.speaker: Leandro
session_5.text: Will do. I'm also planning to give the workshop a proper clean on Friday. There's so much grease on the floor by the stand that I nearly slipped yesterday.

session_5.speaker: Ffion
session_5.text: Ha, please don't do yourself an injury. The shop first opened in 2011 and I swear some of that grease has been there since the very first week.

session_5.speaker: Leandro
session_5.text: That doesn't surprise me at all. I'll bring a stiff brush and some degreaser and see what I can shift.

session_5.speaker: Ffion
session_5.text: Brilliant, I'll buy us both a coffee on Friday as a reward. Right, I'm going to see if that van has finally moved.

session_5.speaker: Leandro
session_5.text: Good luck! Shout if you need me to go out and glare at the driver.

session_6.speaker: Ffion
session_6.text: Morning Leandro. Did you get a chance to look at the kettle? It's making that grinding noise again.

session_6.speaker: Leandro
session_6.text: Yeah I had a go yesterday. I think it's just limescale, I ran vinegar through it twice and it's quieter now.

session_6.speaker: Ffion
session_6.text: Brilliant, you're a hero. I was about to give up and buy a new one.

session_6.speaker: Leandro
session_6.text: Don't throw it out yet, give it a week. If it starts again we'll bin it.

session_6.speaker: Ffion
session_6.text: Deal. How was the afternoon, by the way? I felt bad leaving you on your own with the man who came in about the wheel.

session_6.speaker: Leandro
session_6.text: Ha, the one who kept insisting it was our fault the rim was bent? He came back twice. I just kept nodding and offering to look at it again.

session_6.speaker: Ffion
session_6.text: That's about the best you can do with him. He did the same to me last year, it's never anyone's fault but ours.

session_6.speaker: Leandro
session_6.text: He left in a better mood in the end, said he'd think about it. I'm not holding my breath.

session_6.speaker: Ffion
session_6.text: Fair enough. Anyway, I wanted to ask about the window. I'm thinking it's looking tired, the same bikes have been in there since February.

session_6.speaker: Leandro
session_6.text: Agreed, it's a bit flat. The sun's bleached that cardboard backdrop too, it's gone sort of beige.

session_6.speaker: Ffion
session_6.text: Spring display, then. Something with a bit of colour, maybe a couple of bikes angled towards the street instead of lined up like soldiers.

session_6.speaker: Leandro
session_6.text: I like that. I could grab some plants from the market on Saturday and put a few round the wheels, makes it look less like a warehouse.

session_6.speaker: Ffion
session_6.text: Yes please, keep the receipt and I'll sort you out. Nothing too fussy though, we don't want anything dripping on the paintwork.

session_6.speaker: Leandro
session_6.text: Plastic pots on a tray, nothing dripping. I'll sketch it out and send you a photo before I move anything.

session_6.speaker: Ffion
session_6.text: Perfect. I'll be in after lunch, so leave the old display until I'm there and we'll do it together.

session_6.speaker: Leandro
session_6.text: Sounds good. I'll put the kettle on for when you arrive, assuming it survives.

session_7.speaker: Ffion
session_7.text: Morning! Did you see the road race went right past the end of our street on Saturday? Half the riders looked like they were suffering already.

session_7.speaker: Leandro
session_7.text: Ha, I caught the tail end of it on my way in. Someone had a puncture right outside the bakery and I nearly ran out with a pump.

session_7.speaker: Ffion
session_7.text: You should have! Free advertising. Anyway, are you still up for the charity ride next month?

session_7.speaker: Leandro
session_7.text: Definitely, I've already told my cousin he's coming too. He hasn't ridden in years so I'll be waiting for him at every hill.

session_7.speaker: Ffion
session_7.text: Good, bring snacks then. I thought we could do a little tune-up stand at the start for anyone with squeaky brakes.

session_7.speaker: Leandro
session_7.text: Nice idea. Oh, before I forget, I was sorting the paperwork folder yesterday and the rent letter came through, so the shop's monthly rent is now $1,950.

session_7.speaker: Ffion
session_7.text: Ah, right. I'd been expecting something like that, thanks for flagging it. I'll sort it out with the accounts this week.

session_7.speaker: Leandro
session_7.text: No rush, I just didn't want it sitting in the folder. How did the afternoon go yesterday, by the way? I left before the man with the folding bike came back.

session_7.speaker: Ffion
session_7.text: Oh, don't. He came back twice and argued that the fault was the road, not his bike. Then he asked for a discount for his trouble.

session_7.speaker: Leandro
session_7.text: Classic. Did you give him one?

session_7.speaker: Ffion
session_7.text: Not a penny, but I did give him a cup of tea so he'd stop sighing at the counter. He left almost smiling.

session_7.speaker: Leandro
session_7.text: That's your superpower, honestly. I'd have just handed him the spanner and said good luck.

session_7.speaker: Ffion
session_7.text: Oh, one good bit of news, a new e-bike arrived in stock this morning: the Trek Verve. It's sitting by the window if you want to have a look.

session_7.speaker: Leandro
session_7.text: Nice, I'll pop it on a stand and give it a proper once-over after lunch. The window display could do with something shiny anyway.

session_7.speaker: Ffion
session_7.text: Perfect. Maybe wipe off the fingerprints from the last customer who pressed his nose against the glass.

session_7.speaker: Leandro
session_7.text: Will do. I'll leave the nose prints on the charity ride poster though, that's part of its charm.

session_8.speaker: Ffion
session_8.text: Morning Leandro. The kettle's finally died, I've been boiling water in a saucepan like a caveman.

session_8.speaker: Leandro
session_8.text: Ha, I wondered why the tea tasted faintly of burnt metal yesterday. We could just grab a cheap one from the shop on the corner.

session_8.speaker: Ffion
session_8.text: Good plan, I'll pick one up at lunch. Also there's a delivery van parked right across our door again.

session_8.speaker: Leandro
session_8.text: I saw that. The driver was just standing there on his phone, so I knocked on his window and he moved eventually.

session_8.speaker: Ffion
session_8.text: Brilliant, thank you. By the way, for the order sheet, our inner tubes come from Tandem Supply Co, so put that down for the next batch.

session_8.speaker: Leandro
session_8.text: Okay, noted. Are we still doing the big clean of the workshop today or is it too busy?

session_8.speaker: Ffion
session_8.text: Let's do it, the floor by the stands is covered in old grease and bits of rubber. I'll sort the bench if you take the floor.

session_8.speaker: Leandro
session_8.text: Deal. I'll get the degreaser and the stiff brush out, that stuff never comes off with just a mop.

session_8.speaker: Ffion
session_8.text: Wait, I've got something wrong, scrap what I said earlier. Our inner-tube supplier isn't Tandem Supply Co, that was a mistake on my part. It's Spindle & Co.

session_8.speaker: Leandro
session_8.text: Ah, glad you said before I filled anything in. I'll cross the other one out.

session_8.speaker: Ffion
session_8.text: Thanks. I always muddle the two names when I'm tired.

session_8.speaker: Leandro
session_8.text: Easily done. Right, I'm starting on the floor, the van's gone now so at least we can prop the door open for the fumes.

session_8.speaker: Ffion
session_8.text: Good call. Fresh air will help, and I'll put the saucepan on for tea once we're done.

session_8.speaker: Leandro
session_8.text: Perfect. Should I sweep the corner behind the tool wall too? There's years of dust back there.

session_8.speaker: Ffion
session_8.text: Yes please, if you can face it. Wear a mask, it's properly grim behind there.

session_8.speaker: Leandro
session_8.text: Will do. I'll message you when it's finished and we can celebrate with the worst cup of tea ever.

session_9.speaker: Ffion
session_9.text: Morning! I finally changed the window display last night. Took me ages to get the wheel garland to hang straight.

session_9.speaker: Leandro
session_9.text: Oh nice, I saw it on my way past. It looks really good from the street, very eye-catching.

session_9.speaker: Ffion
session_9.text: Thanks. Quick thing before I forget: the till software we use is TillPoint, so if you're ever stuck at the counter, that's the one to look up.

session_9.speaker: Leandro
session_9.text: Okay, good to know. I'll keep that in mind for when it freezes on me again.

session_9.speaker: Ffion
session_9.text: Wait, sorry, I got that wrong. It's not TillPoint, that was a mistake on my part. The till software we use is ShopKeep One.

session_9.speaker: Leandro
session_9.text: Ha, no worries. Thanks for catching it.

session_9.speaker: Ffion
session_9.text: How's the workshop looking? I was thinking we should do a proper deep clean this week.

session_9.speaker: Leandro
session_9.text: Honestly it's overdue. There's chain grease on practically every surface, and the floor by the stand is properly black.

session_9.speaker: Ffion
session_9.text: Right, let's do it Tuesday when it's quiet. Kofi is our lead mechanic, so I'll ask him to sort the tool wall while we scrub the floor.

session_9.speaker: Leandro
session_9.text: Sounds like a plan. I'll bring some extra rags and that degreaser spray.

session_9.speaker: Ffion
session_9.text: Perfect. Have you had many people in with punctures since the roadworks started on the high street?

session_9.speaker: Leandro
session_9.text: Loads. Three came in on Saturday alone, all picked up glass or bits of grit from the diggings.

session_9.speaker: Ffion
session_9.text: Ugh, I thought so. Maybe we should put a little sign up reminding people to check their tyres after riding through there.

session_9.speaker: Leandro
session_9.text: Good idea, I can write one up this afternoon and stick it by the door.

session_9.speaker: Ffion
session_9.text: Oh, and one more thing: a new e-bike arrived in stock this morning, the red Cube. It's still in the back, so give it a wipe down before it goes on the floor.

session_9.speaker: Leandro
session_9.text: Will do! I'll get it set up tomorrow and tuck it in near the window.

session_10.speaker: Ffion
session_10.text: Morning Leandro! Did you see the charity ride is happening next month? Half the village seems to have signed up already.

session_10.speaker: Leandro
session_10.text: I saw the poster in the cafe window. I might do the shorter loop if my knees agree to it.

session_10.speaker: Ffion
session_10.text: Ha, your knees are twenty-six, they'll cope. I'm thinking of offering free tyre checks for anyone riding it.

session_10.speaker: Leandro
session_10.text: Good idea, people always turn up with soft tyres and a prayer. We could do it the Saturday before.

session_10.speaker: Ffion
session_10.text: Done, I'll put it on the chalkboard. Oh, and the red Cube was sold, a guy came in yesterday afternoon and rode away on it after about ten minutes.

session_10.speaker: Leandro
session_10.text: Ah nice, that one had been sitting by the window for ages. The gap in the display looks odd now though.

session_10.speaker: Ffion
session_10.text: I'll shuffle things round tomorrow so it doesn't look so bare. Did you hear about the local race, by the way?

session_10.speaker: Leandro
session_10.text: The one up on the hill road? My mate Dai is entering, he's been training like mad and boring everyone about it.

session_10.speaker: Ffion
session_10.text: Tell him to pop in beforehand and I'll check his brakes. That climb is nasty on the descent.

session_10.speaker: Leandro
session_10.text: Will do. Speaking of nasty, I've had so many punctures coming in since the roadworks started on the high street.

session_10.speaker: Ffion
session_10.text: Same here, three people this week alone. All of them said there was grit and bits of metal left in the gutter.

session_10.speaker: Leandro
session_10.text: I rode through it on Friday and picked up a sliver of glass. Took me ages to find it in the tyre.

session_10.speaker: Ffion
session_10.text: Maybe we should ring the council and ask them to sweep it properly. It's costing everyone a fortune in patches.

session_10.speaker: Leandro
session_10.text: Good call, I'll email them this afternoon if you like. Might get a faster reply from the shop address than from me.

session_10.speaker: Ffion
session_10.text: Yes, use the shop one, thanks. I'll bring biscuits in tomorrow as a thank you for covering the counter.

session_10.speaker: Leandro
session_10.text: Now you're talking. See you in the morning!

session_11.speaker: Ffion
session_11.text: Morning Leandro! Did you manage to sort the kettle out? It was making that awful rattling noise again yesterday.

session_11.speaker: Leandro
session_11.text: Morning! I descaled it last night, so it should be quieter now. Fingers crossed, otherwise it's going in the bin.

session_11.speaker: Ffion
session_11.text: Ha, brilliant. I'll test it with a proper cuppa as soon as I'm in.

session_11.speaker: Leandro
session_11.text: Oh, before I forget, we ship the online orders with Dropswift now. The old courier stopped collecting from us, so I switched it over on Thursday.

session_11.speaker: Ffion
session_11.text: Good to know, thanks for sorting that. Are the labels printing okay?

session_11.speaker: Leandro
session_11.text: Yep, printed three this morning without any trouble. Easier than before, honestly.

session_11.speaker: Ffion
session_11.text: Lovely. Are you still coming along to the charity ride on Saturday week? I promised the organisers we'd have someone on hand for punctures.

session_11.speaker: Leandro
session_11.text: Definitely, I'll bring the pump and a bag of patches. Do you think I'll need the track pump too, or just the mini one?

session_11.speaker: Ffion
session_11.text: Bring both, people always turn up with soft tyres. And we do rent bikes out, so a few folks might ask us about hiring one on the day.

session_11.speaker: Leandro
session_11.text: Good point, I'll make a little sign for the van so people know. Might even get a few new faces in the shop out of it.

session_11.speaker: Ffion
session_11.text: Fingers crossed. Right, the workshop is a state again, there's oil on the floor and the bench is buried.

session_11.speaker: Leandro
session_11.text: I can do a proper clean this afternoon once the morning rush dies down. I'll do the degreaser tray and sweep under the stands as well.

session_11.speaker: Ffion
session_11.text: You're a star. Oh, and the Orbea Vibe came in this morning, so it's sitting by the window now.

session_11.speaker: Leandro
session_11.text: Nice, it looks smart in the photos. I'll wipe it down and put it out front once the workshop is done.

session_11.speaker: Ffion
session_11.text: Perfect. See you in a bit, and save me a decent mug if that kettle behaves!

session_11.speaker: Leandro
session_11.text: Will do, see you soon!

session_12.speaker: Ffion
session_12.text: Morning Leandro! Did you see the turnout for the local race on Saturday? The whole high street was lined with people.

session_12.speaker: Leandro
session_12.text: I did, I walked past on my way to the bakery. Loads of kids on the sidelines banging pots and pans, it was brilliant.

session_12.speaker: Ffion
session_12.text: Ha, sounds about right. Oh, before I forget, we're shipping the online orders with Harrier Post now, so the old labels in the drawer are no good any more.

session_12.speaker: Leandro
session_12.text: Got it, I'll bin the old ones and keep an eye out for the new packaging. Do I need to do anything different when I book a pickup?

session_12.speaker: Ffion
session_12.text: Nope, same routine, just a different name on the box. Pretty painless really.

session_12.speaker: Leandro
session_12.text: Good. Are we still on for the charity ride next month? I'm trying to talk my brother into coming along.

session_12.speaker: Ffion
session_12.text: Definitely. I'd love to get a decent group from the shop together, maybe we could set up a little water stop outside the door as it passes.

session_12.speaker: Leandro
session_12.text: Great idea. I can bring a few folding chairs and a banner if you've got spare card to make a sign.

session_12.speaker: Ffion
session_12.text: I've got plenty of card. Also, a bit of admin news: the rent on the shop is $2,800 a month now, so I'll be watching the budget a little closer.

session_12.speaker: Leandro
session_12.text: Ah, fair enough. Let me know if there's anything I can do on my end to help keep costs down.

session_12.speaker: Ffion
session_12.text: Will do, thanks. Honestly just keep being brilliant with the customers and we'll be fine.

session_12.speaker: Leandro
session_12.text: Easy enough. Oh, the kettle in the back is making that rattling noise again, I think the element is going.

session_12.speaker: Ffion
session_12.text: Ugh, that kettle has been through the wars. I'll grab a new one this week, we can't be without tea.

session_12.speaker: Leandro
session_12.text: Honestly it's the most important piece of equipment in the building. Right after the pump, maybe.

session_12.speaker: Ffion
session_12.text: Ha, agreed. By the way, the Cannondale Tesoro turned up this morning, it's the new one in the corner by the window.

session_12.speaker: Leandro
session_12.text: Oh nice, I'll go and give it a wipe down and put the tag on it. Cuppa first, assuming the kettle survives the morning!

session_13.speaker: Ffion
session_13.text: Morning! How did the weekend go in the shop? I only managed to pop in on Saturday afternoon.

session_13.speaker: Leandro
session_13.text: Busy, mostly. We had a run of punctures come in, all from people who'd ridden through the roadworks on the main road.

session_13.speaker: Ffion
session_13.text: Ha, I had a feeling that would happen. Was it all glass and bits of grit?

session_13.speaker: Leandro
session_13.text: Mostly little flints and a couple of staples. One guy had three in the same tyre, he was not thrilled.

session_13.speaker: Ffion
session_13.text: Poor thing. Did you put a note by the till about checking tyres for embedded bits before fitting a new tube? Saves people coming straight back.

session_13.speaker: Leandro
session_13.text: Yeah, I stuck one up on Friday. Most people actually read it, which surprised me.

session_13.speaker: Ffion
session_13.text: Good. Oh, and Saoirse is the lead mechanic now, so if anything technical comes up while I'm out, ask her first. Anyway, did the man with the creaky bottom bracket ever come back?

session_13.speaker: Leandro
session_13.text: He did, and he was a nightmare. Said we hadn't fixed it, then admitted he'd been riding a different bike the whole time.

session_13.speaker: Ffion
session_13.text: Oh no, classic. Did he at least apologise?

session_13.speaker: Leandro
session_13.text: Sort of. He muttered something and bought a bottle of chain lube on the way out, so I'll count that as a win.

session_13.speaker: Ffion
session_13.text: Ha, a peace offering. By the way, the Trek Verve was sold on Saturday, just before I left. Can you take it off the website and the window card?

session_13.speaker: Leandro
session_13.text: Nice one, will do this morning. Was it the lady who'd been back twice to look at it?

session_13.speaker: Ffion
session_13.text: That's the one. She finally decided, and she was really happy with it.

session_13.speaker: Leandro
session_13.text: Great. I was thinking of giving the workshop a proper clean on Wednesday when it's quiet, the floor by the stand is properly black.

session_13.speaker: Ffion
session_13.text: Yes please, that would be brilliant. Just don't throw out the old rags in the blue box, I use those for the mudguards.

session_13.speaker: Leandro
session_13.text: Ha, noted, blue box stays. I'll shove everything else on the shelves into the cupboard while I mop.

session_14.speaker: Ffion
session_14.text: Morning! Did you see the road closures for Saturday's race? The whole high street is going to be taped off by nine.

session_14.speaker: Leandro
session_14.text: Yeah, I saw the notice on the lamppost. Should be a good crowd though, maybe a few people will wander in.

session_14.speaker: Ffion
session_14.text: Fingers crossed. I might put a sign out front just in case.

session_14.speaker: Leandro
session_14.text: Good idea. Oh, by the way, the rent on the shop has changed, it's now $2,100 a month. Letter came through yesterday.

session_14.speaker: Ffion
session_14.text: Ah, right. Thanks for letting me know, I'll sort it out when I'm in tomorrow.

session_14.speaker: Leandro
session_14.text: No rush, it doesn't start till next month anyway.

session_14.speaker: Ffion
session_14.text: Okay good. Anyway, the workshop is a state. I was thinking we could do a proper clean on Friday afternoon.

session_14.speaker: Leandro
session_14.text: Fine by me. The floor by the back bench is properly grim, there's chain oil everywhere.

session_14.speaker: Ffion
session_14.text: Ha, I know. I'll bring some of that degreaser spray from home, it works better than what we've got.

session_14.speaker: Leandro
session_14.text: Perfect. I'll sort the tool wall while I'm at it, half the spanners are in the wrong spots.

session_14.speaker: Ffion
session_14.text: You're a star. Is the kettle still doing that weird clicking thing?

session_14.speaker: Leandro
session_14.text: Worse, now it takes ages to boil and then switches off halfway. I think it's finally dying.

session_14.speaker: Ffion
session_14.text: Ugh. I'll grab a new one on my way in, can't run a workshop without tea.

session_14.speaker: Leandro
session_14.text: Definitely not. Get a cheap one though, ours gets descaled about once a year.

session_14.speaker: Ffion
session_14.text: Ha, fair point. Right, I'll see you tomorrow, I'll bring biscuits too.

session_14.speaker: Leandro
session_14.text: Brilliant, see you then!

session_15.speaker: Ffion
session_15.text: Morning! Did you see the window display when you came past? I swapped the helmets around yesterday evening.

session_15.speaker: Leandro
session_15.text: I did, looks much better. The blue ones catch the light nicely now.

session_15.speaker: Ffion
session_15.text: Good, that was the idea. Though I couldn't hang the banner properly because of that delivery van parked right across the door.

session_15.speaker: Leandro
session_15.text: Ha, I saw it this morning too. The driver was nowhere to be found for ages, I had to squeeze in sideways with the bags.

session_15.speaker: Ffion
session_15.text: Typical. Is the kettle behaving, by the way? It was making a weird clicking noise on Thursday.

session_15.speaker: Leandro
session_15.text: Still clicking, but it boils. I'd give it another month before it gives up completely.

session_15.speaker: Ffion
session_15.text: I'll pick up a new one if it dies. Can't run this place without tea.

session_15.speaker: Leandro
session_15.text: Agreed. Oh, a customer asked me yesterday what we charge, and I told him a basic service is $55, which is what it's always been.

session_15.speaker: Ffion
session_15.text: Right. Anyway, I moved the little stand with the bells closer to the counter, did you notice?

session_15.speaker: Leandro
session_15.text: I did, people keep picking them up and ringing them. Constant jingling all afternoon.

session_15.speaker: Ffion
session_15.text: Good for sales, bad for my ears. Someone rang on the phone yesterday asking about hiring a bike for the weekend, by the way.

session_15.speaker: Leandro
session_15.text: Oh, what did you tell them?

session_15.speaker: Ffion
session_15.text: That we've stopped offering rentals. They were a bit disappointed but said they'd try elsewhere.

session_15.speaker: Leandro
session_15.text: Fair enough. Want me to move the display stand away from the window so the sun doesn't fade the boxes?

session_15.speaker: Ffion
session_15.text: Yes please, and put the kettle on while you're back there. I'll take the van driver a stern look when he finally turns up.

session_15.speaker: Leandro
session_15.text: Deal. Tea first, stern looks second.

session_16.speaker: Ffion
session_16.text: Morning! Did you see the sign-up numbers for the charity ride? Way more than last year.

session_16.speaker: Leandro
session_16.text: I did, it's looking great. I think the new route through the villages helped, people like a bit of scenery.

session_16.speaker: Ffion
session_16.text: Agreed. I'm thinking of putting a little repair stand at the halfway stop, just in case anyone gets a puncture or a loose chain.

session_16.speaker: Leandro
session_16.text: Good idea. I can run it if you like, I don't mind giving up a Saturday morning for that.

session_16.speaker: Ffion
session_16.text: You're a star. Honestly I need the break from yesterday, that customer who came in twice about the same squeaky brake was a lot.

session_16.speaker: Leandro
session_16.text: Oh no, the one in the green jacket? He cornered me last week too and kept insisting the squeak was our fault.

session_16.speaker: Ffion
session_16.text: That's him. I checked it three times and it was fine, I think he just likes a chat and a complaint.

session_16.speaker: Leandro
session_16.text: Probably lonely, bless him. Still, I'm not volunteering for round three.

session_16.speaker: Ffion
session_16.text: Fair enough, I'll take him next time. Are you riding in the local race next weekend, by the way?

session_16.speaker: Leandro
session_16.text: Thinking about it. My legs aren't convinced yet, I've barely trained since the summer got busy.

session_16.speaker: Ffion
session_16.text: Ha, same excuse every year and then you finish in the top ten anyway.

session_16.speaker: Leandro
session_16.text: Top fifteen at best! But yes, I'll probably enter. It's only a few laps round the park.

session_16.speaker: Ffion
session_16.text: Go on then, I'll come and heckle from the finish line with a flask of tea.

session_16.speaker: Leandro
session_16.text: Deal. If I'm last, you're buying the cake afterwards.

session_16.speaker: Ffion
session_16.text: If you're last I'll buy two. Right, I'd better unlock the stockroom, talk later!

session_16.speaker: Leandro
session_16.text: Speak soon, and I'll sort the repair stand kit before the ride.
